usage_tip: Hindi speakers often say 'became to be'; English needs only 'became'.

simple_explanation: To make something different or become different. When something changes, it becomes different from how it was before -- this could be a small adjustment or a big transformation.
example_1: I need to change my plans for tomorrow.
example_2: The weather changed suddenly in the afternoon.
example_3: She changed her hairstyle for the new year.
collocations: change your mind, change plans, sudden change, change for the better
related_phrasal_verbs: change into, change up, switch around
where_it_s_used: Weather, opinions, plans, personal growth, technology
action_sequence: Before: things are one way → During: something happens → After: they are different
grammar_pattern: change + noun (change your mind) / change from X to Y
common_mistake: I will change this shirt with a bigger size.
correct_version: I will change this shirt for a bigger size.
why_it_s_wrong: To exchange something, use 'change it FOR something else', not 'with'.
pronunciation_tip: Rhymes with "range" and "strange" -- stress on the single syllable.
etymology: From Old French "changier," from Latin "cambiare" (to exchange, barter) -- the same root as "exchange."
prefix_root_suffix: no clear prefix/root/suffix breakdown -- from Latin "cambiare"
mnemonic: CHANGE contains "ANGE" like "arrange" -- when you change something, you rearrange it into something new.
memory_trick: CHANGE: C for Coins — you get change after paying.
visual_association: A caterpillar's cocoon slowly opening into something new.
emotion_feel: Neutral, sometimes uncertainty or hope depending on context
difference_explained: Change = make different. Exchange = give one thing and get another. 'Change clothes'; 'exchange a gift'.
mini_conversation:
A: Are we still meeting at 5?
B: Actually, can we change it to 6? Something came up.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character stares at an old photo and says softly, "Everything has changed since that summer."
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials announced major changes to the city's public transport system."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I've really changed my mind about moving abroad."
mcq_options: A) To stay the same forever  B) To become or make different  C) To copy exactly  D) To repeat something
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The plan might ______ if it rains tomorrow. → change
find_and_fix_to_correct: She is change her job next month. → She is changing her job next month. (need "-ing" form after "is" for present continuous)
translate: मौसम अचानक बदल गया। → The weather suddenly changed.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you would like to change in your routine.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to make something different or become different'?
usage_tip: 'Change' as a noun also means coins: 'Keep the change.'

simple_explanation: To become bigger, taller, or more developed over time. "Grow" describes something increasing in size, age, or amount over time -- plants grow, children grow, and even businesses or feelings can grow.
example_1: These tomatoes grow very fast in summer.
example_2: He has grown three inches this year.
example_3: The company grew rapidly after the new product launch.
collocations: grow up, grow rapidly, grow taller, grow stronger
related_phrasal_verbs: grow up, grow apart, grow into
action_sequence: Before: plant a seed → During: water it daily → After: it becomes a plant
grammar_pattern: grow + adjective (grow tired) / grow + noun phrase (grow tomatoes)
common_mistake: She has grow a lot since last year.
correct_version: She has grown a lot since last year.
why_it_s_wrong: After 'has', use the past participle 'grown'.
pronunciation_tip: Rhymes with "know" and "show" -- the "ow" makes a long "O" sound.
spelling_tip: G-R-O-W; past tense is irregular: grow -> grew -> grown.
etymology: From Old English "growan" (to grow, flourish, thrive), a common Germanic word related to "green" -- both describe living things flourishing.
prefix_root_suffix: no clear prefix/root/suffix breakdown -- from Old English "growan"
mnemonic: GROW rhymes with "glow" -- plants GROW and seem to GLOW with new leaves.
memory_trick: GROW → GREW → GROWN, like THROW → THREW → THROWN.
visual_association: A small seedling stretching upward into a tall plant.
difference_explained: Grow = get bigger (plants, numbers, people). Grow up = become an adult (only people).
mini_conversation:
A: Wow, your daughter has really grown!
B: I know, she's grown so fast this year.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A father looks at his son and says, "I still remember when you were this small -- look how much you've grown."
news_style_line: News-style: "The economy is expected to grow by three percent this year."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I can't believe how much your garden has grown since spring."
mcq_options: A) To become smaller  B) To become bigger or develop over time  C) To stop completely  D) To break apart
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: This plant will ______ much taller if you water it daily. → grow
find_and_fix_to_correct: The plant grow very quickly in this soil. → The plant grows very quickly in this soil. (third-person singular needs "-s")
translate: यह पेड़ हर साल तेज़ी से बढ़ता है। → This tree grows quickly every year.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a plant or vegetable you have grown.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become bigger, taller, or more developed over time'?
usage_tip: 'Grow up' = become an adult. 'What do you want to be when you grow up?'

simple_explanation: To grow, improve, or become more advanced over time. When something develops, it grows or changes gradually into a more advanced, complete, or complex form -- this applies to skills, countries, plans, or even health conditions.
example_1: She wants to develop her English skills.
example_2: The company developed a new app for students.
example_3: Children develop language skills quickly at this age.
collocations: develop skills, rapidly develop, develop a plan, fully developed
related_phrasal_verbs: build up, grow into, come along
where_it_s_used: Education, business, technology, health, personal growth
action_sequence: Before: start with a basic skill → During: practise and improve → After: become advanced
grammar_pattern: develop + noun (develop a habit / develop new technology)
common_mistake: I want to develop my English since long time.
correct_version: I have wanted to develop my English for a long time.
why_it_s_wrong: For something continuing up to now, use the present perfect with 'for': 'have wanted… for a long time'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the second syllable: dih-VEL-uhp.
etymology: From Old French "desveloper" (des- "un-" + voloper "to wrap") -- literally "to unwrap" or "unfold," extended to mean "to bring out or grow gradually."
mnemonic: DE-VELOP sounds like "unwrap an envelope" -- to develop something is to slowly unwrap and reveal it.
memory_trick: DEVELOP: a photo develops slowly from nothing to a clear picture.
visual_association: A blueprint slowly transforming into a finished building.
difference_explained: Improve = make better. Develop = grow over time, or build something new (develop an app).
mini_conversation:
A: How's the new project going?
B: We're still developing the design, but it's coming along well.
everyday_scene: Everyday: An inventor looks over blueprints and says, "We've been developing this idea for three years -- it's finally ready."
news_style_line: News-style: "Scientists are developing a new vaccine that could be ready within a year."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I'm trying to develop better study habits before exams start."
mcq_options: A) To destroy something completely  B) To grow or improve gradually  C) To copy something exactly  D) To forget a skill
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Our team is working hard to ______ a new mobile application. → develop
find_and_fix_to_correct: The country is develop very fast these years. → The country is developing very fast these years. (need "-ing" form after "is" for present continuous)
translate: वह अपने संचार कौशल को विकसित करना चाहती है। → She wants to develop her communication skills.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a skill you want to develop this year.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to grow, improve, or become more advanced over time'?
usage_tip: 'Developing country' and 'app developer' are common phrases.

simple_explanation: To become larger in number or amount, or to make something larger. When something increases, its size, amount, or level goes up -- prices, populations, and skills can all increase.
example_2: The company increased salaries by ten percent.
example_3: Traffic has increased a lot since last summer.
collocations: increase significantly, sharply increase, increase in demand, gradual increase
related_phrasal_verbs: go up, build up, ramp up
action_sequence: Before: the price is ₹100 → During: it goes up → After: it becomes ₹110
grammar_pattern: increase + by/to + amount (increase by 20% / increase to $50)
common_mistake: The price increased to 10 percent.
correct_version: The price increased by 10 percent.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'by' for the amount of change and 'to' for the final number.
pronunciation_tip: Verb: in-CREASE. Noun: IN-crease. The stress shift changes the part of speech.
spelling_tip: Remember "crease" at the end -- like a fold that grows bigger.
etymology: From Latin "increscere" (in- "into" + crescere "to grow") -- the same root as "crescent" and "crescendo."
mnemonic: IN-CREASE sounds like things "creasing" and expanding outward -- to increase is to grow bigger, like an expanding crease.
memory_trick: INCREASE: IN + CREASE: more folds, more size.
visual_association: An arrow on a graph rising steadily upward.
emotion_feel: Neutral, sometimes optimism when the increase is positive
difference_explained: Increased BY 10% = the change. Increased TO ₹110 = the new total.
mini_conversation:
A: How's business been lately?
B: Really good -- our sales increased almost 30% this quarter.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A businessman points at a chart and announces, "Our numbers have increased every single quarter this year."
news_style_line: News-style: "The report shows a sharp increase in online shopping over the past year."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I've noticed my energy has really increased since I started exercising."
mcq_options: A) To become smaller  B) To become larger in amount or number  C) To stay exactly the same  D) To disappear completely
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The demand for electric cars has ______ significantly this year. → increased
find_and_fix_to_correct: The population increase rapidly last decade. → The population increased rapidly last decade. (past tense needed for a completed past action)
translate: पिछले साल कंपनी की बिक्री में काफी वृद्धि हुई। → The company's sales increased a lot last year.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a price that increased recently.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become larger in number or amount, or to make something larger'?
usage_tip: Verb: in-CREASE. Noun: IN-crease ('a big increase').

simple_explanation: To become smaller in number or amount, or to make something smaller. When something decreases, its size, amount, or level goes down -- the opposite of increasing.
example_2: The population has decreased over the past decade.
example_3: Doctors advised him to decrease his salt intake.
collocations: decrease significantly, sharply decrease, decrease in value, gradual decrease
related_phrasal_verbs: go down, drop off, taper off
action_sequence: Before: the price is ₹100 → During: it goes down → After: it becomes ₹80
grammar_pattern: decrease + by/to + amount (decrease by 15% / decrease to 100 units)
common_mistake: The company decreased their prices to 20 percent.
correct_version: The company decreased their prices by 20 percent.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'by' for the amount of change and 'to' for the final number.
spelling_tip: Notice it shares "crease" with "increase" -- just add "de-" instead of "in-."
etymology: From Latin "decrescere" (de- "down, away" + crescere "to grow") -- the opposite of "increase," literally "to grow downward."
mnemonic: DE-CREASE -- the "DE" (down) makes things CREASE inward and shrink, the opposite of increase.
memory_trick: DE-CREASE: 'de' = down.
visual_association: An arrow on a graph sloping steadily downward.
emotion_feel: Neutral, sometimes relief or concern depending on context
difference_explained: Decrease can happen by itself (sales decreased). Reduce is usually done by someone (we reduced costs).
mini_conversation:
A: How are the store's sales this month?
B: They've actually decreased a bit compared to last month.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A scientist frowns at a chart and says, "The readings have decreased far more than we expected."
news_style_line: News-style: "Crime rates have decreased significantly in the city over the last five years."
casual_conversation: Casual: "My stress levels have really decreased since I started meditating."
mcq_options: A) To become larger  B) To become smaller in amount or number  C) To stay the same  D) To completely disappear
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The number of visitors to the park has ______ this winter. → decreased
find_and_fix_to_correct: The temperature decrease rapidly last night. → The temperature decreased rapidly last night. (past tense needed for a completed past action)
translate: पिछले महीने कंपनी के मुनाफे में कमी आई। → The company's profit decreased last month.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something that decreased in your city.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become smaller in number or amount, or to make something smaller'?
usage_tip: Verb: de-CREASE. Noun: DE-crease.

simple_explanation: To become better, or to make something better. When you improve, you get better at something over time, often through practice, effort, or fixing what was wrong before.
example_1: My English has improved a lot this year.
example_2: She practiced daily to improve her guitar skills.
example_3: The new manager improved the team's morale.
collocations: improve significantly, gradually improve, improve skills, room for improvement
related_phrasal_verbs: come along, level up, get better
where_it_s_used: Education, health, business, sports, personal development
action_sequence: Before: have a weak skill → During: practise regularly → After: the skill gets better
grammar_pattern: improve + noun (improve your writing) / improve on + something (improve on last attempt)
common_mistake: I want to improve of my speaking skills.
correct_version: I want to improve my speaking skills.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Improve' takes a direct object, with no 'of'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the second syllable: im-PROOV.
etymology: From Anglo-French "emprower" (to turn to profit), related to Old French "prou" (profit/advantage) -- originally about making land more profitable, later broadened to "make better."
prefix_root_suffix: im- (variant of "en-," to make) + prove (from Old French "prou," profit)
mnemonic: IM-PROVE sounds like "prove" -- when you improve, you PROVE you can do better.
memory_trick: IM-PROVE: PROVE yourself a little better each day.
visual_association: A shaky pencil line transforming into a smooth, confident stroke.
difference_explained: Improve = make better in quality. Increase = make bigger in number or amount.
mini_conversation:
A: How's your Spanish coming along?
B: It's improving slowly -- I can hold basic conversations now.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A young athlete finally beats their personal best and yells, "I've improved so much since last season!"
news_style_line: News-style: "Air quality has improved noticeably since the new regulations took effect."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Honestly, your cooking has really improved since last year."
mcq_options: A) To become worse  B) To become better  C) To stay exactly the same  D) To completely stop
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Practicing every day will help you ______ your pronunciation. → improve
find_and_fix_to_correct: She improved her English since two years. → She has improved her English over the last two years. (use present perfect with "over/for," not simple past with "since two years")
translate: नियमित अभ्यास से उसकी लेखन क्षमता में सुधार हुआ। → Regular practice improved her writing skills.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about how you improved your English this year.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become better, or to make something better'?
usage_tip: 'Room for improvement' = it's OK, but could be better.

simple_explanation: To become bigger or to make something bigger, especially in size or area. When something expands, it grows outward or increases in size, area, or scope -- businesses expand into new markets, and metal expands when heated.
example_1: The company plans to expand into Asia.
example_2: Metal expands when it gets hot.
example_3: The city has expanded rapidly over the last decade.
collocations: expand rapidly, expand into, plan to expand, expand your knowledge
related_phrasal_verbs: branch out, grow bigger, spread out
action_sequence: Before: a shop is small → During: it opens more branches → After: it covers a bigger area
grammar_pattern: expand + into + area/market (expand into new markets)
common_mistake: The company wants to expand to three new countries next year.
correct_version: The company wants to expand into three new countries next year.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'expand INTO' for new markets or areas.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the second syllable: ik-SPAND.
spelling_tip: E-X-P-A-N-D -- remember "pand" like "panda" but with a "D."
etymology: From Latin "expandere" (ex- "out" + pandere "to spread") -- literally "to spread out."
mnemonic: EX-PAND sounds like "expand a fan" -- you open a folded fan outward, just like something expands outward.
memory_trick: EX-PAND: PAN out, spread wider.
visual_association: A balloon slowly stretching bigger as air fills it.
difference_explained: Expand = get bigger in all directions. Extend = get longer (in time or one direction).
mini_conversation:
A: I heard your bakery is doing really well.
B: Yes, we're planning to expand to a second location next year.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A founder points to a map covered in pins and says, "This is where we're going to expand next."
news_style_line: News-style: "The airline announced plans to expand its routes to five new cities."
casual_conversation: Casual: "We're thinking of expanding the kitchen once we save enough money."
mcq_options: A) To become smaller  B) To grow bigger or spread out  C) To stop completely  D) To repeat exactly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The business hopes to ______ into new international markets next year. → expand
find_and_fix_to_correct: The metal expand when you heat it. → The metal expands when you heat it. (third-person singular needs "-s")
translate: कंपनी अगले साल यूरोप में अपना विस्तार करना चाहती है। → The company wants to expand into Europe next year.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a business that expanded to new cities.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become bigger or to make something bigger, especially in size or area'?
usage_tip: 'Expand on' = give more detail: 'Can you expand on that point?'

simple_explanation: To become smaller, especially in size. When something shrinks, it gets smaller than it was before -- clothes can shrink in hot water, and economies or populations can shrink too.
example_1: My sweater shrank in the wash.
example_2: The economy shrank during the recession.
example_3: Wool sweaters often shrink if washed in hot water.
collocations: shrink dramatically, shrink in the wash, shrinking population, continue to shrink
action_sequence: Before: wash a cotton shirt in hot water → During: it gets smaller → After: it no longer fits
grammar_pattern: shrink + (by/to) + amount (shrink by two sizes)
common_mistake: My shirt has shrinked after washing.
correct_version: My shirt has shrunk after washing.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Shrink' is irregular: shrink – shrank – shrunk.
spelling_tip: S-H-R-I-N-K -- remember it's irregular: shrink, shrank, shrunk.
etymology: From Old English "scrincan" (to shrivel, contract), a Germanic word related to "scrimp" -- describing something pulling inward and becoming smaller.
prefix_root_suffix: no clear prefix/root/suffix breakdown -- from Old English "scrincan"
mnemonic: SHRINK rhymes with "sink" -- when clothes shrink in the wash, they seem to sink inward and get smaller.
memory_trick: SHRINK → SHRANK → SHRUNK, like DRINK → DRANK → DRUNK.
visual_association: A balloon slowly deflating and getting smaller.
difference_explained: Shrink = get smaller by itself, often in size. Reduce = make smaller on purpose.
mini_conversation:
A: Why is your favorite T-shirt so tight now?
B: I accidentally shrank it in the dryer.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character holds up a tiny sweater and groans, "I can't believe this shrank that much in one wash."
news_style_line: News-style: "The country's economy shrank for the second quarter in a row."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Careful with that shirt -- it shrinks if you put it in the dryer."
mcq_options: A) To become bigger  B) To become smaller  C) To stay the same size  D) To change color
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: If you wash wool in hot water, it will probably ______. → shrink
find_and_fix_to_correct: The population have shrinked over the years. → The population has shrunk over the years. (correct past participle is "shrunk," and use "has" for singular "population")
translate: बार-बार धोने से यह ऊनी स्वेटर सिकुड़ गया। → This wool sweater shrank from being washed repeatedly.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about clothes that shrank in the wash.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become smaller, especially in size'?
usage_tip: 'Shrink' is also informal for a psychiatrist.

simple_explanation: To change completely into something very different. When something transforms, it undergoes a dramatic, often total change in appearance, nature, or character -- much bigger than a small change.
example_1: The old factory was transformed into apartments.
example_2: Technology has transformed the way we communicate.
example_3: The caterpillar transforms into a butterfly.
collocations: completely transform, transform into, transform your life, digital transformation
action_sequence: Before: see an old building → During: renovate it completely → After: it becomes a modern café
grammar_pattern: transform + noun + into + noun (transform the room into an office)
common_mistake: The old house was transformed to a modern café.
correct_version: The old house was transformed into a modern café.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'transform into', not 'transform to'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the second syllable: trans-FORM.
spelling_tip: Notice "form" inside "trans-FORM" -- the shape (form) is what changes.
etymology: From Latin "transformare" (trans- "across, beyond" + formare "to shape") -- literally "to change shape completely."
mnemonic: TRANS-FORM = "form" changes across (trans) to something new -- a complete change of shape or identity.
memory_trick: TRANS-FORM: change across to a new FORM, like Transformers.
visual_association: A gray caterpillar bursting into a vividly colored butterfly.
difference_explained: Change can be small. Transform means a complete, dramatic change.
mini_conversation:
A: I barely recognized this neighborhood!
B: I know, it's been completely transformed in the last few years.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A dull, gray building lights up at night, and a character gasps, "It's completely transformed -- I can't believe this is the same place."
news_style_line: News-style: "The new policy is expected to transform how small businesses access funding."
casual_conversation: Casual: "This app has honestly transformed the way I manage my time."
mcq_options: A) To stay exactly the same  B) To change completely into something different  C) To slightly adjust something  D) To destroy something permanently
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The renovation completely ______ the old warehouse into a modern gallery. → transformed
find_and_fix_to_correct: Her attitude transformed to more positive. → Her attitude transformed into something more positive. (use "into," not "to")
translate: तकनीक ने हमारे संवाद करने के तरीके को पूरी तरह बदल दिया है। → Technology has completely transformed the way we communicate.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a place near you that has transformed.
