reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at a time before now or before another event'?
usage_tip: 'As I said earlier' refers back to something already said.

simple_explanation: Before now, or sooner than expected. "Already" shows that something has happened before this moment, often earlier than you expected.
example_1: I have already finished my homework.
example_2: She has already left for the airport.
example_3: We already ate dinner, thanks.
collocations: already done, already know, already finished, already gone
where_it_s_used: Completed tasks, surprises, confirming something happened, impatience
grammar_pattern: subject + have/has + already + past participle (I have already eaten.) / subject + be + already + adjective (She is already tired.)
common_mistake: I already have finished my work.
correct_version: I have already finished my work.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Already' goes between 'have' and the past participle.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the second syllable: awl-RED-ee.
spelling_tip: One word -- ALREADY, not "all ready" (a different phrase meaning fully prepared).
etymology: From Middle English "al" (all) + "ready" -- literally "completely ready," evolving to mean something has happened before now or sooner than expected.
prefix_root_suffix: al- (all) + ready (prepared) = compound adverb ("completely ready/before now")
word_family: all (determiner), ready (adj.) -- built from two existing words, no further derived forms
mnemonic: ALREADY = ALL + READY -- it's already done, all set before you even asked.
memory_trick: AL-READY: ALL READY — done before now.
visual_association: A checklist with every box already ticked off before you even started.
difference_explained: Already = before now. All ready = everyone or everything is prepared.
mini_conversation:
A: Don't forget to call the doctor.
B: I already did -- the appointment's on Friday.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character checks their watch and says, "We're already late -- let's go!"
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials confirmed the new bridge is already ahead of schedule."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I already told you three times -- please listen this time."
mcq_options: A) Before now, sooner than expected  B) Not yet happened  C) Never going to happen  D) At the same time every day
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She has ______ finished reading the whole book. → already
find_and_fix_to_correct: Have you finished already your homework? → Have you already finished your homework? (place "already" right after the subject "you," before the main verb)
translate: मैंने पहले से ही अपना काम पूरा कर लिया है। → I have already finished my work.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you've already done today.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'before now, or sooner than expected'?
usage_tip: 'Already?' shows surprise that something happened so soon.

simple_explanation: Continuing up to now; not yet finished or changed. "Still" shows that a situation continues without change, up to the present moment -- something that was true before is true now too.
example_1: She still lives in her hometown.
example_2: He's still working on the report.
example_3: I still don't understand this rule.
collocations: still waiting, still here, still working, not yet still
related_phrasal_verbs: up to now, as of yet
where_it_s_used: Ongoing situations, unfinished tasks, unresolved feelings
grammar_pattern: subject + still + verb (He still plays football.) / subject + be + still + adjective (She is still tired.)
common_mistake: I still not understand this lesson.
correct_version: I still don't understand this lesson.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Still' doesn't replace the negative; you still need 'don't'.
spelling_tip: Double "l" at the end -- STIL + L.
etymology: From Old English "stille" (motionless, quiet) -- originally meant "without movement," extended to mean "continuing up to now" or "even so."
prefix_root_suffix: no clear prefix/root/suffix breakdown -- a simple base adverb from Old English
word_family: no clear derived forms -- "still" also functions as a noun/adjective meaning "motionless" in other contexts
mnemonic: STILL means something hasn't stopped -- it's STILL going, STILL standing.
memory_trick: STILL: time is STILL going, like a still river.
visual_association: A candle that keeps burning, still lit long after it was expected to go out.
synonyms: yet, even now, up to now
difference_explained: Still = continuing (I'm still waiting). Yet = up to now, in negatives and questions (not yet).
mini_conversation:
A: Have you finished packing?
B: No, I'm still working on it.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character sighs, "I still can't believe he actually did that."
news_style_line: News-style: "Rescue crews are still searching the area for survivors."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Are you still awake? It's almost midnight."
mcq_options: A) Continuing up to now  B) Never happened  C) Happening only once  D) Happening in the distant past
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He ______ hasn't replied to my message from yesterday. → still
find_and_fix_to_correct: She still is waiting for the bus. → She is still waiting for the bus. (place "still" after the verb "is," not before it)
translate: वह अभी भी अपने पुराने घर में रहता है। → He still lives in his old house.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you still don't understand.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'continuing up to now; not yet finished or changed'?
usage_tip: 'Still' also means not moving: 'Sit still.'

simple_explanation: At a later time, after something else has happened. "Afterward" refers to a time following an event that was just mentioned -- it connects two events in a sequence.
example_1: We had dinner, and afterward we watched a movie.
example_2: The rain stopped, and afterward the sun came out.
example_3: She studied hard and, afterward, passed the exam easily.
collocations: shortly afterward, soon afterward, and afterward
where_it_s_used: Storytelling, sequences of events, describing plans
grammar_pattern: event 1, and afterward + event 2 (We ate, and afterward we relaxed.)
common_mistake: Afterward the movie, we ate dinner.
correct_version: After the movie, we ate dinner.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Afterward' can't be followed by a noun. Use 'after' + noun.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: AF-ter-werd.
etymology: From Old English "æfterweard" ("æfter" = after + "-weard" = in the direction of) -- literally "in a direction following," meaning at a later time.
prefix_root_suffix: after (root, following) + -ward = suffix meaning "in the direction of"
mnemonic: AFTERWARD = AFTER + WARD (direction) -- moving forward in time, after something else.
memory_trick: AFTER-WARD: toward the AFTER time.
visual_association: One event finishing and a new scene starting right after it.
difference_explained: After + noun (after the movie). Afterward alone (we ate afterward).
mini_conversation:
A: What did you do after the meeting?
B: We grabbed lunch afterward and talked more.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character recalls, "We laughed all night, and afterward, everything felt lighter."
news_style_line: News-style: "The ceremony concluded, and afterward guests gathered for a reception."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Let's grab a coffee, and afterward we can walk through the park."
mcq_options: A) At a later time, following an event  B) Before an event begins  C) During an event  D) Never
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: They finished the exam and, ______, celebrated together. → afterward
find_and_fix_to_correct: Afterward we ate, we watched TV. → After we ate, we watched TV. (use the conjunction "after," not "afterward," before a clause)
translate: हमने खाना खाया, और उसके बाद हम टहलने गए। → We had dinner, and afterward we went for a walk.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence using 'afterwards' about a meal.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at a later time, after something else has happened'?
usage_tip: UK: 'afterwards'. US: 'afterward'. Both correct.

simple_explanation: Before something happens; in advance. "Beforehand" describes doing or knowing something in advance of an event, so you're prepared when it happens.
example_2: We booked our tickets beforehand to avoid the rush.
example_3: He always checks the weather beforehand.
collocations: plan beforehand, know beforehand, prepare beforehand
grammar_pattern: subject + verb + beforehand (Please call beforehand.)
common_mistake: Please tell me beforehand about the party, before it starts.
correct_version: Please tell me beforehand about the party.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Beforehand' already means 'before it happens', so the extra clause repeats it.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: bih-FOR-hand.
spelling_tip: One word -- BEFORE + HAND, no hyphen.
etymology: From "before" + "hand" -- literally "before at hand," meaning done or prepared in advance of an event.
prefix_root_suffix: before (root) + hand (root) = compound adverb ("ready in advance")
word_family: before (prep./adv./conj.), hand (n.) -- built from two existing words
mnemonic: BEFOREHAND means you prepare things BEFORE they're needed, with your HAND already ready.
memory_trick: BEFORE-HAND: BEFORE the HAND needs it.
visual_association: A suitcase packed and ready the night before a trip.
synonyms: in advance, ahead of time, previously
difference_explained: Before + noun (before the party). Beforehand alone (tell me beforehand).
related_words: in advance, ahead of time, previously, in preparation
mini_conversation:
A: I didn't know you were vegetarian!
B: Sorry, I should have told you beforehand.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A planner reminds the team, "Let's confirm everything beforehand so nothing goes wrong."
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials advised residents to prepare emergency kits beforehand, ahead of storm season."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Can you send me the agenda beforehand so I can prepare?"
mcq_options: A) In advance, before something happens  B) After an event ends  C) During an event  D) Never
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: We should book the restaurant ______ since it gets crowded. → beforehand
find_and_fix_to_correct: I informed to him beforehand about the change. → I informed him beforehand about the change. ("inform" takes a direct object without "to" -- "inform someone," not "inform to someone")
translate: उसने पार्टी से पहले ही मुझे सूचित कर दिया था। → He informed me beforehand about the party.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you should do beforehand for an exam.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'before something happens; in advance'?
usage_tip: 'Let me know beforehand' = tell me in advance.

simple_explanation: At the same time, while something else is happening. "Meanwhile" connects two events that are happening at the same time, often used to shift focus from one thing to another in a story.
example_1: I cooked dinner; meanwhile, she set the table.
example_2: The kids played outside; meanwhile, their parents prepared lunch.
example_3: He studied for exams; meanwhile, his sister practiced piano.
collocations: meanwhile back at, meanwhile in another part of, meanwhile elsewhere
related_phrasal_verbs: at the same time, in the meantime
where_it_s_used: Storytelling, narration, describing parallel events, news reports
grammar_pattern: sentence 1; meanwhile, + sentence 2 (She cooked; meanwhile, he cleaned.)
common_mistake: Meanwhile she was cooking, he was cleaning.
correct_version: While she was cooking, he was cleaning.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Meanwhile' starts a new sentence. To join two clauses, use 'while'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: MEEN-wyl.
spelling_tip: One word -- MEAN + WHILE, no space or hyphen.
etymology: From Middle English "mene while" ("mean" = in between + "while" = a period of time) -- literally "in the time between," describing simultaneous events.
prefix_root_suffix: mean- (in between) + while (a period of time) = compound adverb
word_family: while (n./conj.), mean (adj., a different meaning) -- built from existing words, no further derived forms
mnemonic: MEANWHILE connects two things happening at the same time, in the WHILE between events.
memory_trick: MEAN-WHILE: in the WHILE between.
visual_association: A split-screen showing two different scenes happening at once.
synonyms: in the meantime, simultaneously, at the same time
difference_explained: While + clause joins two things (while she cooked, he cleaned). Meanwhile starts a new sentence.
related_words: simultaneously, at the same time, in the meantime, concurrently
mini_conversation:
A: What's happening with the renovation?
B: The kitchen is almost done. Meanwhile, we're living out of boxes in the living room.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A narrator shifts scenes: "Meanwhile, across town, someone else was making a very different choice."
news_style_line: News-style: "Meanwhile, officials in the capital held emergency talks over the crisis."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I'll finish the dishes; meanwhile, can you put the kids to bed?"
mcq_options: A) At the same time as another event  B) A long time before  C) Never at the same time  D) Only once a year
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She packed the bags; ______, he loaded the car. → meanwhile
find_and_fix_to_correct: Meanwhile that he cooked, she cleaned the house. → While he cooked, she cleaned the house. (use "while" to join the two clauses -- "meanwhile" doesn't connect clauses this way)
translate: वह खाना बना रही थी; इसी बीच, उसने घर की सफ़ाई की। → She was cooking food; meanwhile, he cleaned the house.
write_your_own_sentence: Write two sentences using 'Meanwhile' to link them.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at the same time, while something else is happening'?
usage_tip: 'In the meantime' means the same.

simple_explanation: At the present time, as compared to the past. "Nowadays" is used to talk about the present time, especially when comparing it to how things used to be.
example_2: Nowadays, people shop online more than in stores.
example_3: Nowadays, fewer people write letters by hand.
collocations: nowadays most people, nowadays it seems, unlike nowadays
related_phrasal_verbs: in this day and age, these days
where_it_s_used: Comparing past and present, technology, social trends, lifestyle changes
grammar_pattern: Nowadays, + sentence (Nowadays, everyone has a phone.) / subject + verb + nowadays (People travel more nowadays.)
common_mistake: Nowadays people used to text more than call.
correct_version: Nowadays, people text more than they call.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Nowadays' is about the present, so don't use 'used to'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: NOW-uh-days.
spelling_tip: One word -- NOW + A + DAYS, no hyphens.
etymology: From "now" + "adays" (an old plural form of "day," as in "always") -- literally "in these days," describing the present era compared to the past.
prefix_root_suffix: now (root) + a- (linking vowel) + days (plural of day) = compound adverb ("in these days")
word_family: now (adv.), day (n.) -- built from existing words, no further derived forms
mnemonic: NOWADAYS = NOW + DAYS -- how things are these days, in modern times.
memory_trick: NOW-A-DAYS: in these DAYS NOW.
visual_association: An old photograph placed next to a modern smartphone.
emotion_feel: Neutral, sometimes nostalgic when comparing to the past
synonyms: these days, currently, in modern times
difference_explained: Same meaning. 'These days' is more informal.
related_words: currently, these days, in modern times, presently
mini_conversation:
A: Do kids still play outside much?
B: Not as much nowadays -- they're usually on their phones.
everyday_scene: Everyday: An elderly character remarks, "Nowadays, everything moves so much faster than it used to."
news_style_line: News-style: "Nowadays, more households are switching to renewable energy sources."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Nowadays, I barely watch TV -- I just stream everything."
mcq_options: A) At the present time, compared to the past  B) A long time ago  C) Never  D) Only on weekends
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ______, almost everyone owns a mobile phone. → Nowadays
find_and_fix_to_correct: Nowadays, people are more busier than before. → Nowadays, people are busier than before. (don't use "more" together with the "-er" comparative form "busier")
translate: आजकल ज़्यादातर लोग ऑनलाइन शॉपिंग करते हैं। → Nowadays, most people shop online.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something people do nowadays that they didn't before.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at the present time, as compared to the past'?
usage_tip: Common in essays: 'Nowadays, most people…'.

simple_explanation: Once a year; every year. "Annually" describes something that happens on a yearly basis, once every twelve months.
example_1: The company holds its meeting annually.
example_2: The festival is held annually in the spring.
example_3: She gets a health check-up annually.
collocations: held annually, annually reviewed, meet annually, paid annually
related_phrasal_verbs: once a year, year after year
where_it_s_used: Events, reports, subscriptions, celebrations, official schedules
grammar_pattern: subject + verb + annually (The event takes place annually.)
common_mistake: We meet annually every year for the conference.
correct_version: We meet annually for the conference.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Annually' already means every year.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: AN-yoo-uh-lee.
spelling_tip: Remember "annu-" as in "anniversary" -- ANNU + AL + LY.
etymology: From "annual" (Latin "annualis," from "annus," year) + "-ly" -- describing something happening once every year.
word_family: annual (adj./n.), annuity (n., a related financial term)
mnemonic: ANNUALLY happens every year, like an ANNUAL birthday celebration.
memory_trick: ANNUAL-LY: ANNUS = year.
visual_association: A calendar with the same date circled every single year.
synonyms: yearly, once a year, every year
difference_explained: Same meaning. Annually is more formal.
mini_conversation:
A: How often does the town hold this festival?
B: Annually, every August.
everyday_scene: Everyday: An organizer announces, "This festival has been held annually for over twenty years."
news_style_line: News-style: "The company reported its earnings annually, showing steady growth."
casual_conversation: Casual: "We renew our gym membership annually to save some money."
mcq_options: A) Once a year  B) Once a month  C) Every single day  D) Never
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The award ceremony takes place ______ in December. → annually
find_and_fix_to_correct: The magazine is publish annually. → The magazine is published annually. (use the past participle "published" in this passive construction, not the base form "publish")
translate: यह उत्सव हर साल सर्दियों में मनाया जाता है। → This festival is celebrated annually in winter.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you do annually.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'once a year; every year'?
usage_tip: 'Annual' is the adjective: 'annual leave', 'annual report'.

simple_explanation: Happening once every week. When something is weekly, it happens on a regular schedule, one time each week, like a class or a payment.
example_1: We meet weekly to review progress.
example_2: The magazine is published weekly.
example_3: He gets paid weekly instead of monthly.
collocations: weekly meeting, weekly report, paid weekly, weekly schedule
related_phrasal_verbs: on a weekly basis, week in week out
grammar_pattern: verb + weekly (We meet weekly) or weekly + noun (a weekly report)
common_mistake: I go to the gym weekly three times.
correct_version: I go to the gym three times a week.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Weekly' means once a week; for other numbers, say 'three times a week'.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables, stress on the first: WEEK-lee.
etymology: "Week" (Old English "wice") + "-ly" adverb/adjective suffix meaning "happening every week."
prefix_root_suffix: week = root (seven-day period) + -ly = adverb/adjective suffix ("happening every...")
mnemonic: WEEKLY = once every WEEK, LY marks how often.
memory_trick: WEEK-LY: once a WEEK.
visual_association: A calendar page with the same day circled every seven days.
difference_explained: Same meaning. For more than once, say 'twice a week'.
mini_conversation:
A: How often does the team newsletter come out?
B: It comes out weekly, every Friday morning.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A manager reminds the team, "Remember, status updates are due weekly, no exceptions."
news_style_line: News-style: "The committee announced it will publish updated figures on a weekly basis."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I do my grocery shopping weekly, usually on Sundays."
mcq_options: A) Once a year  B) Once a week  C) Once a day  D) Once a month
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The gym holds a ______ yoga class every Tuesday. → weekly
find_and_fix_to_correct: We have a weekly meeting every two weeks. → We have a biweekly meeting every two weeks. ("weekly" means every week, not every two weeks)
translate: हमारी टीम की बैठक साप्ताहिक होती है। → Our team meeting is weekly.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you do weekly.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'happening once every week'?
usage_tip: 'Weekly' is also an adjective: 'a weekly meeting'.

simple_explanation: In a fast way, without delay. When you do something quickly, you do it in a short amount of time, with speed.
example_2: He quickly grabbed his umbrella before the rain started.
example_3: Please reply quickly - the offer ends today.
collocations: react quickly, quickly realize, move quickly, quickly become
related_phrasal_verbs: hurry up, speed up, rush through
grammar_pattern: verb + quickly (He ran quickly) or quickly + verb (She quickly answered)
common_mistake: He drives very quick on this road.
correct_version: He drives very quickly on this road.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he drives, use the adverb 'quickly'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: KWIK-lee.
etymology: From Old English "cwic" (alive, lively) -> "quick" (fast) + "-ly."
mnemonic: QUICKLY - picture a "quick" click of your fingers, done in no time.
memory_trick: QUICK + LY: adjective + LY = adverb.
visual_association: A blurred figure sprinting past a clock.
difference_explained: Fast is both adjective and adverb (drive fast). 'Fastly' does not exist.
mini_conversation:
A: The bus is leaving in two minutes!
B: Okay, I'm coming - let me just grab my bag quickly.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character glances at the clock and says, "We need to move quickly, we're almost out of time."
news_style_line: News-style: "Emergency crews responded quickly after the alarm was raised."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Can you quickly check if I left my phone in the car?"
mcq_options: A) In a fast way  B) In a careful way  C) In a loud way  D) In a slow way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He ______ closed the window when it started to rain. → quickly
find_and_fix_to_correct: She learns things very quick. → She learns things very quickly.
translate: कृपया जल्दी से यह फॉर्म भरें। → Please fill out this form quickly.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you do quickly in the morning.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a fast way, without delay'?
usage_tip: 'As quickly as possible' = as fast as you can.

simple_explanation: At a low speed, not fast. When you do something slowly, you take your time and don't rush.
example_1: The old man walked slowly across the street.
example_2: Please speak slowly - I'm still learning English.
example_3: The traffic moved slowly during rush hour.
collocations: move slowly, speak slowly, slowly but surely, walk slowly
grammar_pattern: verb + slowly (He drove slowly) or slowly + verb (She slowly nodded)
common_mistake: Please drive more slow.
correct_version: Please drive more slowly.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how to drive, use the adverb 'slowly'.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: SLOH-lee - the "w" blends into the "oh" sound.
etymology: From Old English "slaw" (sluggish, lazy) + "-ly."
mnemonic: SLOWLY - stretch the word out as you say it... sloooow-ly.
memory_trick: SLOW + LY: adjective + LY = adverb.
visual_association: A snail inching along a leaf.
emotion_feel: Calm, sometimes impatience if it's unwanted
difference_explained: Slow = adjective (a slow car). Slowly = adverb (drive slowly). 'Go slow' is informal.
mini_conversation:
A: I can't understand your accent very well.
B: Sorry, let me say that again, more slowly.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character warns, "Back away slowly, don't make any sudden moves."
news_style_line: News-style: "Recovery efforts are proceeding slowly due to difficult weather conditions."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Could you explain that again, but a bit more slowly this time?"
mcq_options: A) At a fast speed  B) At a low speed  C) In a loud way  D) In a careful way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The queue moved so ______ that we waited for an hour. → slowly
find_and_fix_to_correct: He eats very slow. → He eats very slowly.
translate: कृपया धीरे-धीरे बोलिए, मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा। → Please speak slowly, I don't understand.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence asking someone to speak more slowly.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at a low speed, not fast'?
usage_tip: 'Slowly but surely' = gradually but steadily.

simple_explanation: Paying close attention so as not to make a mistake or cause damage. When you do something carefully, you focus and go slowly enough to avoid mistakes or accidents.
example_1: She carefully wrapped the glass vase.
example_2: Read the instructions carefully before you start.
example_3: He carefully placed the baby in the crib.
collocations: listen carefully, read carefully, carefully planned, handle carefully
related_phrasal_verbs: watch out, look out, take care
where_it_s_used: Safety instructions, handling objects, driving, studying
grammar_pattern: verb + carefully (She checked carefully) or carefully + past participle (a carefully planned trip)
common_mistake: She is careful listening to the teacher.
correct_version: She is carefully listening to the teacher.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how she listens, use the adverb 'carefully'.
pronunciation_tip: Four syllables: CARE-fuh-lee - stress on the first syllable.
etymology: "Care" (Old English "caru," worry/attention) + "-ful" (full of) + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: care = root + -ful = suffix (full of) + -ly = adverb suffix
mnemonic: CAREFULLY = full of CARE - picture someone holding an egg with both hands.
memory_trick: CAREFUL + LY: double L.
visual_association: Someone carrying a full cup of tea without spilling a drop.
difference_explained: Careful = adjective (be careful). Carefully = adverb (drive carefully).
mini_conversation:
A: This package says 'fragile' on it.
B: Okay, I'll carry it carefully.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A surgeon says quietly, "Everyone stay calm, we do this carefully, step by step."
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials asked residents to carefully follow the evacuation instructions."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Please handle these dishes carefully, they were a gift."
mcq_options: A) In a fast way  B) With attention, to avoid mistakes  C) In a loud voice  D) Without thinking
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He ______ folded the letter and put it in the envelope. → carefully
find_and_fix_to_correct: Please listen careful to the announcement. → Please listen carefully to the announcement.
translate: कृपया इस दस्तावेज़ को ध्यान से पढ़ें। → Please read this document carefully.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you do carefully.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'paying close attention so as not to make a mistake or cause damage'?
usage_tip: 'Handle carefully' is printed on fragile boxes.

simple_explanation: Without enough attention or thought, in a way that can cause mistakes. When you do something carelessly, you rush or don't pay attention, so you're more likely to make an error.
example_1: He carelessly left the door unlocked.
example_2: She carelessly threw her bag on the wet floor.
example_3: The report was written carelessly, full of typos.
collocations: act carelessly, spend money carelessly, carelessly discarded, carelessly written
related_phrasal_verbs: mess up, slip up, throw together
grammar_pattern: verb + carelessly (He worked carelessly)
common_mistake: He drives careless.
correct_version: He drives carelessly.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he drives, use the adverb 'carelessly'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on the first syllable: CARE-lis-lee.
etymology: "Care" + "-less" (without) + "-ly" - literally "without care."
mnemonic: CARELESSLY = CARE is LESS - the opposite of paying attention.
memory_trick: CARELESS + LY: CARE-LESS-LY.
visual_association: Papers scattered messily across a desk after being tossed down.
difference_explained: Careless = adjective (a careless driver). Carelessly = adverb (drives carelessly).
mini_conversation:
A: The vase is broken again!
B: Yeah, someone carelessly knocked it off the shelf.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A detective mutters, "Whoever did this left the evidence carelessly out in the open."
news_style_line: News-style: "Inspectors found that safety equipment had been carelessly stored, violating regulations."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I carelessly left my keys on the bus again."
mcq_options: A) With great attention  B) Without enough attention  C) Very slowly  D) Very politely
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He ______ tossed his coat onto the chair without looking. → carelessly
find_and_fix_to_correct: He carelessly did check his work before submitting. → He carelessly submitted his work without checking it.
translate: उसने लापरवाही से चाबी कहीं रख दी और अब ढूंढ नहीं पा रहा। → He carelessly put his keys down somewhere and can't find them now.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something done carelessly.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'without enough attention or thought, in a way that can cause mistakes'?
usage_tip: 'Carelessly' often goes with mistakes and accidents.

simple_explanation: Making very little or no noise. When you do something quietly, you avoid making sound so you don't disturb anyone.
example_1: The children played quietly in their room.
example_2: He quietly closed the door so he wouldn't wake the baby.
example_3: She quietly slipped out of the meeting.
collocations: quietly sit, speak quietly, quietly leave, quietly wait
related_phrasal_verbs: keep it down, sneak out, tiptoe around
grammar_pattern: verb + quietly (She spoke quietly)
common_mistake: Please walk quiet when you enter the room.
correct_version: Please walk quietly when you enter the room.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how you walk, use the adverb 'quietly'.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: KWY-uht-lee - stress on the first syllable.
etymology: From Latin "quietus" (at rest, calm) + "-ly."
mnemonic: QUIETLY - picture a librarian with a finger to her lips, saying "shh."
memory_trick: QUIET + LY: QUIET-LY — not 'quitely'.
visual_association: Someone tiptoeing across a wooden floor at night.
difference_explained: Quietly = without noise. Quite = fairly. Different spelling and sound.
mini_conversation:
A: The baby just fell asleep.
B: Okay, I'll close the door quietly.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A soldier signals to his team, "Move quietly, they don't know we're here yet."
news_style_line: News-style: "The new policy was quietly introduced without a formal announcement."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Can you talk more quietly? People are trying to study."
mcq_options: A) With a lot of noise  B) With very little noise  C) Very quickly  D) Very angrily
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She ______ closed her laptop so no one would notice she was leaving early. → quietly
find_and_fix_to_correct: He talks so quiet that I can't hear him. → He talks so quietly that I can't hear him.
translate: बच्चे चुपचाप कमरे में खेल रहे थे। → The children were playing quietly in the room.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about where you have to move quietly.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'making very little or no noise'?
usage_tip: 'Quietly confident' = sure, but not loud about it.

simple_explanation: Making a lot of noise; not quietly. When you do something loudly, the sound is strong and easy for others to hear, sometimes too easy.
example_1: The crowd cheered loudly for the team.
example_2: He laughed so loudly that everyone turned to look.
example_3: Please don't play music loudly after 10 PM.
collocations: laugh loudly, speak loudly, loudly complain, music playing loudly
grammar_pattern: verb + loudly (They cheered loudly)
common_mistake: He talked very loud during the exam.
correct_version: He talked very loudly during the exam.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he talked, use the adverb 'loudly'.
spelling_tip: "Loud" + "ly" - no changes needed to the base word.
etymology: From Old English "hlud" (making a strong sound) + "-ly."
mnemonic: LOUDLY - imagine turning the volume dial all the way up, LOUD and clear.
memory_trick: LOUD + LY: adjective + LY.
visual_association: A stadium crowd roaring with hands cupped around their mouths.
emotion_feel: Energy, excitement, or annoyance depending on context
difference_explained: Loudly = with a lot of noise. Aloud = so others can hear (not silently).
mini_conversation:
A: I couldn't hear the announcement at all.
B: Really? They said it pretty loudly through the speakers.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character bangs on the table and shouts loudly, "This meeting is over!"
news_style_line: News-style: "Protesters chanted loudly outside the government building for several hours."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Sorry, could you speak a bit more loudly? I can barely hear you."
mcq_options: A) With very little sound  B) With a lot of sound  C) With great care  D) Very slowly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The fans cheered so ______ that the players could hear them from the field. → loudly
find_and_fix_to_correct: Don't talk so loud in the library. → Don't talk so loudly in the library.
translate: वह इतनी ज़ोर से हँसा कि पूरा कमरा सुन सकता था। → He laughed so loudly that the whole room could hear.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about someone who speaks loudly on the phone.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'making a lot of noise; not quietly'?
usage_tip: 'Out loud' is also used: 'Read it out loud.'

hindi_meaning: धीरे से, नरमी से, कोमलता से
simple_explanation: In a soft, mild, and careful way. When you do something gently, you use light force and a soft touch so you don't hurt or startle anyone.
example_1: She gently rocked the baby to sleep.
example_2: He gently placed his hand on her shoulder.
example_3: Please close the door gently.
collocations: gently remind, gently touch, gently push, gently ask
where_it_s_used: Caring for children/pets, medical care, kindness, physical handling
grammar_pattern: verb + gently (He touched it gently)
common_mistake: She gentle patted the dog on the head.
correct_version: She gently patted the dog on the head.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe the action, use the adverb 'gently'.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: JENT-lee - the "g" is soft, like a "j" sound.
spelling_tip: "Gentle" drops the final "e" before adding "-ly": gentle -> gently.
etymology: From Old French "gentil" (noble, well-born), which came to mean "mild, soft-mannered" in English + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: gentle = root (mild, soft) + -ly = adverb suffix (drop the final "e")
mnemonic: GENTLY - a GENTLE breeze that barely moves the leaves.
memory_trick: GENTLE → GENTLY: drop the E, add Y.
visual_association: A hand cupping a small bird without squeezing it.
difference_explained: Gently = with care, not force. Softly = quietly, or with a light touch.
mini_conversation:
A: The kitten looks scared.
B: Just talk to it gently and it should calm down.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A caretaker whispers, "Just breathe, I'm going to move you gently now."
news_style_line: News-style: "Rescuers gently lifted the injured hiker onto the stretcher."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Can you hold the puppy a bit more gently? He's still small."
mcq_options: A) In a rough, forceful way  B) In a soft, careful way  C) In a very loud way  D) In a fast, hurried way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The mother ______ wiped the tears from her son's face. → gently
find_and_fix_to_correct: He pushed the door gentle. → He pushed the door gently.
translate: उसने धीरे से बच्चे को गोद में उठाया। → She gently picked up the baby.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you handle gently.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a soft, mild, and careful way'?
usage_tip: 'Gently does it' = do it slowly and carefully.

hindi_meaning: खुरदरेपन से, ज़ोर से; लगभग (अनुमानित अर्थ में)
simple_explanation: In a forceful, not gentle way; also used to mean "approximately." "Roughly" usually describes handling something without gentleness, but it's also commonly used before a number to mean "about" or "around."
example_1: He roughly pushed past the crowd.
example_2: Don't handle the plates so roughly - they're old.
example_3: The trip takes roughly two hours.
collocations: roughly handled, roughly speaking, roughly estimated, roughly equal
where_it_s_used: Handling objects, sports, arguments, estimates and numbers
grammar_pattern: verb + roughly (He grabbed it roughly) or roughly + number (roughly 100 people)
common_mistake: The trip costs rough ₹5,000.
correct_version: The trip costs roughly ₹5,000.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Roughly' means 'about' before a number. 'Rough' is the adjective.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: RUHF-lee - the "gh" is pronounced like an "f."
spelling_tip: "Rough" + "ly" - remember the silent "gh" that sounds like "f."
etymology: From Old English "ruh" (hairy, coarse) + "-ly" - originally described rough/coarse texture, extended to rough manner.
mnemonic: ROUGHLY - think of sandpaper: ROUGH and not smooth.
memory_trick: ROUGH-LY: a ROUGH (not exact) figure.
visual_association: A hand shoving a door open instead of pushing it softly.
difference_explained: Same meaning for numbers. Approximately is more formal.
mini_conversation:
A: How far is the station from here?
B: Roughly two kilometers, maybe a 20-minute walk.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A guard grabs the bag roughly and snaps, "Empty your pockets, now."
news_style_line: News-style: "The storm roughly doubled the usual rainfall for this time of year."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Don't grab it so roughly, you'll break the handle."
mcq_options: A) Exactly  B) Approximately, or in a forceful way  C) Never  D) Beautifully
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The renovation should cost ______ two thousand dollars. → roughly
find_and_fix_to_correct: The concert starts on roughly 8 PM. → The concert starts at roughly 8 PM.
translate: वहाँ पहुँचने में लगभग एक घंटा लगेगा। → It will take roughly an hour to get there.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence giving the roughly estimated cost of something.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a forceful, not gentle way; also used to mean "approximately."'?
usage_tip: 'Roughly speaking' = in general terms.

simple_explanation: Without much difficulty or effort. When something happens easily, it doesn't take much work, time, or struggle.
example_1: He can easily solve this puzzle.
example_2: She easily passed the driving test.
example_3: This stain comes off easily with warm water.
collocations: easily accessible, easily available, win easily, easily forget
grammar_pattern: can/could + easily + verb (She could easily finish it)
common_mistake: This puzzle can solve easily.
correct_version: This puzzle can be solved easily.
why_it_s_wrong: The puzzle doesn't solve itself, so use the passive: 'can be solved'.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: EE-zuh-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Easy" changes "y" to "i" before adding "-ly": easy -> easily.
etymology: From Old French "aisie" (comfortable) via "easy" + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: easy = root (comfortable, simple) + -ly = adverb suffix (y -> i before -ly)
mnemonic: EASILY - if it's EASY, you can do it EASILY, without effort.
memory_trick: EASY → EASILY: Y becomes I, add LY.
visual_association: A key sliding smoothly into a lock and turning without resistance.
difference_explained: Easy = adjective (an easy test). Easily = adverb (I passed easily). 'Take it easy' is a fixed phrase.
mini_conversation:
A: Wow, you finished that so fast!
B: Yeah, it was easily the simplest exercise in the book.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A trainer smiles and says, "You've got this - you can easily beat your old record."
news_style_line: News-style: "The proposal was easily approved by a majority vote."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I could easily finish this by tomorrow if you need it sooner."
mcq_options: A) With great difficulty  B) Without much effort  C) Very slowly  D) Very rarely
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She can ______ lift twice her body weight. → easily
find_and_fix_to_correct: He win the race easily yesterday. → He won the race easily yesterday.
translate: वह यह सवाल आसानी से हल कर सकता है। → He can easily solve this question.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you can do easily.

reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'without much difficulty or effort'?
usage_tip: 'Easily' also means 'without doubt': 'easily the best'.

simple_explanation: Almost not at all; barely. "Hardly" means something is true only a very small amount, almost not true - it does NOT mean "in a difficult/forceful way."
example_1: I could hardly hear you over the noise.
example_2: She hardly ever eats fast food.
example_3: He hardly slept last night before the exam.
collocations: hardly ever, hardly any, hardly recognize, can hardly wait
where_it_s_used: Complaints, tiredness, surprise, describing small amounts
grammar_pattern: can/could + hardly + verb (I can hardly believe it) - already negative, don't add "not"
common_mistake: I can't hardly wait for the concert.
correct_version: I can hardly wait for the concert.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Hardly' is already negative, so 'can't hardly' is a double negative.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: HARD-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Hard" + "ly" - looks like a regular "-ly" adverb, but the meaning is not what you'd expect.
etymology: From "hard" + "-ly," but the meaning shifted over centuries from "in a harsh way" to "barely/almost not" - an unusual case of adverb drifting away from its adjective's meaning.
prefix_root_suffix: hard = root + -ly = adverb suffix (meaning has drifted from the base word - an exception to the usual pattern)
mnemonic: HARDLY = "barely" - if you can HARDLY hear someone, you can just BARELY hear them.
memory_trick: HARDLY = almost NOT. It's not the adverb of 'hard'.
visual_association: A nearly empty glass with just one drop of water left.
difference_explained: Hard = with effort (work hard). Hardly = almost not (hardly work).
mini_conversation:
A: Did you sleep well before your flight?
B: Not really, I could hardly sleep at all.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character stumbles in and mutters, "I could hardly stand up after that."
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials say the new policy has hardly changed daily life for most residents."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I've hardly had time to eat lunch today."
mcq_options: A) Very forcefully  B) Almost not at all  C) Very often  D) Extremely well
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: We arrived so late that we could ______ find a parking spot. → hardly
find_and_fix_to_correct: He hardly never calls his parents. → He hardly ever calls his parents. ("hardly never" is a double negative - use "hardly ever")
translate: मुझे मुश्किल से याद है कि मैंने कहाँ चाबियाँ रखीं। → I can hardly remember where I put my keys.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence using 'hardly ever'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'almost not at all; barely'?
usage_tip: 'Hardly ever' = almost never.

hindi_meaning: सुचारू रूप से, आसानी से, बिना रुकावट के
simple_explanation: Without problems, difficulties, or interruptions. When something goes smoothly, everything works well without any trouble along the way.
example_1: The event went smoothly from start to finish.
example_2: The negotiation went smoothly and both sides agreed quickly.
example_3: The new software runs smoothly on older computers.
collocations: run smoothly, go smoothly, transition smoothly, work smoothly together
related_phrasal_verbs: go off without a hitch, sail through
grammar_pattern: verb + smoothly (Everything went smoothly)
common_mistake: The meeting go smooth without any problems.
correct_version: The meeting went smoothly without any problems.
why_it_s_wrong: Use the past 'went' and the adverb 'smoothly'.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: SMOODH-lee - the "th" is voiced, like in "this."
etymology: From Old English "smoðe" (free from roughness) + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: smooth = root (even, without bumps) + -ly = adverb suffix
mnemonic: SMOOTHLY - like ice skating on a SMOOTH surface, no bumps at all.
memory_trick: SMOOTH + LY: no bumps.
visual_association: A car gliding down a freshly paved road with no bumps.
difference_explained: Smooth = adjective (a smooth road). Smoothly = adverb (it went smoothly).
mini_conversation:
A: How did the interview go?
B: Really well, actually - it went smoothly from start to end.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A pilot announces calmly, "We're expecting the flight to go smoothly from here on."
news_style_line: News-style: "Election officials reported that voting proceeded smoothly across the region."
casual_conversation: Casual: "The move went pretty smoothly - we finished by lunchtime."
mcq_options: A) With many problems  B) Without problems or difficulty  C) Very loudly  D) Very slowly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The project ran ______ once everyone agreed on the plan. → smoothly
find_and_fix_to_correct: Everything went smooth during the trip. → Everything went smoothly during the trip.
translate: पूरा कार्यक्रम बिना किसी रुकावट के सुचारू रूप से चला। → The whole event went smoothly without any problems.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about an event that went smoothly.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'without problems, difficulties, or interruptions'?
usage_tip: 'Everything went smoothly' = no problems.

simple_explanation: In an awkward way, without grace or skill, often causing small accidents. When you do something clumsily, your movements are not smooth and you might trip, drop, or bump into things.
example_1: He clumsily knocked over his coffee.
example_2: She clumsily tripped over her own shoelaces.
example_3: The waiter clumsily dropped a tray of glasses.
collocations: clumsily fumble, clumsily dropped, clumsily worded, clumsily handled
related_phrasal_verbs: fumble around, trip up, bump into
grammar_pattern: verb + clumsily (He walked clumsily)
common_mistake: She danced very clumsy at the wedding.
correct_version: She danced very clumsily at the wedding.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how she danced, use the adverb 'clumsily'.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: KLUHM-zuh-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Clumsy" changes "y" to "i" before adding "-ly": clumsy -> clumsily.
etymology: From Middle English "clumsen" (to be numb with cold) -> "clumsy" (awkward, stiff movements) + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: clumsy = root (awkward, stiff) + -ly = adverb suffix (y -> i before -ly)
mnemonic: CLUMSILY - picture someone CLUMSILY knocking over a stack of cups.
memory_trick: CLUMSY → CLUMSILY: Y becomes I.
visual_association: Someone tripping over a shoelace while carrying a stack of boxes.
difference_explained: Clumsy = adjective (a clumsy person). Clumsily = adverb (danced clumsily).
mini_conversation:
A: What happened to your phone screen?
B: I clumsily dropped it while getting out of the car.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character trips over a rug and laughs, "Sorry, I clumsily walk into everything today."
news_style_line: News-style: "The comedy sketch shows an actor clumsily trying to assemble furniture on live television."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I clumsily spilled water all over my notes right before the test."
mcq_options: A) In a graceful, skillful way  B) In an awkward way, causing small accidents  C) In a very quiet way  D) In a confident way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The new intern ______ knocked over the stack of files. → clumsily
find_and_fix_to_correct: He clumsy dropped his phone twice. → He clumsily dropped his phone twice.
translate: वह अनाड़ीपन से सीढ़ियों से लगभग गिर गया। → He clumsily almost fell down the stairs.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you did clumsily.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in an awkward way, without grace or skill, often causing small accidents'?
usage_tip: Often used for dropping or spilling things.

simple_explanation: Without complaining or getting annoyed while waiting or dealing with something difficult. When you act patiently, you stay calm even when something takes a long time or is frustrating.
example_1: She waited patiently for her turn.
example_2: The teacher patiently explained the topic again.
example_3: He patiently answered every question the child asked.
collocations: wait patiently, explain patiently, patiently listen, patiently endure
related_phrasal_verbs: bear with, hold on, stick it out
grammar_pattern: verb + patiently (She listened patiently)
common_mistake: He waited patient for the results.
correct_version: He waited patiently for the results.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he waited, use the adverb 'patiently'.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: PAY-shunt-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Patient" + "ly" - remember the "t" makes a "sh" sound before "ient."
etymology: From Latin "patiens" (suffering, enduring) via "patient" + "-ly."
mnemonic: PATIENTLY - like a PATIENT in a waiting room, calmly waiting their turn.
memory_trick: PATIENT + LY.
visual_association: Someone sitting calmly on a bench, watching the clock without checking it repeatedly.
difference_explained: Patient = adjective (be patient). Patiently = adverb (wait patiently).
mini_conversation:
A: Sorry this is taking so long.
B: It's okay, I'll wait patiently - no rush.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A mentor says gently, "Keep practicing - if you work at it patiently, it'll come."
news_style_line: News-style: "Families waited patiently outside the hospital for updates on the rescue."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Thanks for explaining that so patiently - I finally get it now."
mcq_options: A) In an annoyed, rushed way  B) Calmly, without complaining  C) In a loud voice  D) Very quickly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The doctor ______ answered all of the patient's worried questions. → patiently
find_and_fix_to_correct: She listen patiently to her grandmother's stories every week. → She listens patiently to her grandmother's stories every week.
translate: शिक्षक ने धैर्यपूर्वक हर सवाल का जवाब दिया। → The teacher patiently answered every question.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about a time you waited patiently.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'without complaining or getting annoyed while waiting or dealing with something difficult'?
usage_tip: 'Wait patiently' is common in announcements.

simple_explanation: In a worried or anxious way, often showing physical signs of it. When you do something nervously, you feel anxious or worried, and it often shows in how you move, speak, or look.
example_1: He nervously checked his watch before the interview.
example_2: She nervously bit her nails while waiting for the results.
example_3: He nervously cleared his throat before speaking.
collocations: nervously laugh, nervously wait, nervously glance, nervously fidget
related_phrasal_verbs: bite your nails, break out in a sweat
where_it_s_used: Interviews, exams, first dates, public speaking
grammar_pattern: verb + nervously (She smiled nervously)
common_mistake: He looked nervous around the room before he spoke.
correct_version: He looked around the room nervously before he spoke.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he looked around, use the adverb 'nervously'.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: NUR-vus-lee - stress on the first syllable.
etymology: From Latin "nervosus" (sinewy, vigorous) - meaning shifted over time to describe anxious energy + "-ly."
mnemonic: NERVOUSLY - picture someone's NERVES on edge, hands shaking a little.
memory_trick: NERVOUS + LY.
visual_association: Fingers tapping restlessly on a table while eyes dart toward a doorway.
difference_explained: Nervous = adjective (he looked nervous). Nervously = adverb (he looked around nervously).
mini_conversation:
A: You seem quiet today.
B: Yeah, I'm nervously waiting for my exam results.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character paces the hallway and nervously mutters, "What if they say no?"
news_style_line: News-style: "Investors watched nervously as the markets opened lower than expected."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I was nervously tapping my pen the whole meeting."
mcq_options: A) In a calm, relaxed way  B) In a worried, anxious way  C) In a proud way  D) In a very loud way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She ______ twisted her ring while waiting to be called into the office. → nervously
find_and_fix_to_correct: He nervous laughed when asked the question. → He laughed nervously when asked the question.
translate: वह इंटरव्यू से पहले घबराहट से अपने हाथ मल रहा था। → He was nervously rubbing his hands before the interview.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about how people act nervously before an interview.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a worried or anxious way, often showing physical signs of it'?
usage_tip: 'Laughed nervously' = laughed because of stress.

simple_explanation: In a peaceful, relaxed way, without stress or panic. When you act calmly, you stay relaxed and in control, even in a stressful or difficult situation.
example_1: She calmly explained what had happened.
example_2: He calmly walked the passengers to the exit.
example_3: She calmly answered every difficult question.
collocations: calmly explain, remain calm, respond calmly, calmly wait
grammar_pattern: verb + calmly (She spoke calmly)
common_mistake: He is calm dealing with every problem at work.
correct_version: He calmly deals with every problem at work.
why_it_s_wrong: To describe how he deals with problems, use the adverb 'calmly'.
pronunciation_tip: Two syllables: KAHM-lee - the "l" is often silent or very soft.
spelling_tip: "Calm" + "ly" - the silent "l" stays even though you barely hear it.
etymology: From Old Italian "calma" (heat of the day, stillness) via French, entering English as "calm" + "-ly."
mnemonic: CALMLY - picture a CALM lake, still and quiet, no waves.
memory_trick: CALM + LY: the L in CALM is silent, but both Ls are written.
visual_association: Someone breathing slowly with their eyes closed before a big decision.
difference_explained: Calm = adjective (stay calm). Calmly = adverb (speak calmly).
mini_conversation:
A: The alarm just went off, what do we do?
B: Stay calm - let's walk to the exit calmly, single file.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A flight attendant says calmly over the intercom, "Please remain seated, everything is under control."
news_style_line: News-style: "Officials calmly urged residents not to panic as repairs continued."
casual_conversation: Casual: "Just breathe and try to explain it calmly, one step at a time."
mcq_options: A) In a panicked way  B) In a peaceful, controlled way  C) In a very fast way  D) In a rude way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The teacher ______ handled the noisy classroom without raising her voice. → calmly
find_and_fix_to_correct: Please try to stay calmly during the test. → Please try to stay calm during the test. ("stay" needs the adjective "calm," not the adverb "calmly")
translate: उसने शांति से पूरी स्थिति समझाई। → She calmly explained the whole situation.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about how you calmly handle a problem.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a peaceful, relaxed way, without stress or panic'?
usage_tip: 'Please leave the building calmly' in fire drills.

simple_explanation: In a way that shows strong annoyance or fury. When you do something angrily, your actions or words show that you're upset or furious about something.
example_2: She angrily demanded a refund from the manager.
example_3: He angrily threw his phone onto the couch.
collocations: angrily shout, angrily reply, angrily storm off, angrily demand
related_phrasal_verbs: blow up, snap at, storm off
grammar_pattern: verb + angrily (He shouted angrily)
common_mistake: She was angrily about the broken promise for days.
correct_version: She was angry about the broken promise for days.
why_it_s_wrong: After 'was', use the adjective 'angry', not the adverb.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: ANG-gruh-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Angry" changes "y" to "i" before adding "-ly": angry -> angrily.
etymology: From Old Norse "angr" (grief, distress) via "angry" + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: angry = root (feeling anger) + -ly = adverb suffix (y -> i before -ly)
mnemonic: ANGRILY - picture someone slamming a door ANGRILY after a fight.
memory_trick: ANGRY → ANGRILY: Y becomes I.
visual_association: A red-faced person crossing their arms and turning away sharply.
difference_explained: Angry = adjective (she was angry). Angrily = adverb (she shouted angrily).
mini_conversation:
A: Why did he leave so fast?
B: He angrily stormed out after the manager criticized his work.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A character slams their fist on the desk and angrily shouts, "This is completely unacceptable!"
news_style_line: News-style: "Residents angrily confronted officials over the delayed repairs at the town hall meeting."
casual_conversation: Casual: "He angrily hung up the phone in the middle of the call."
mcq_options: A) In a calm, gentle way  B) In a furious, upset way  C) In a happy way  D) In a quiet way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The driver ______ honked his horn when the light turned green. → angrily
find_and_fix_to_correct: He talk angrily to his brother yesterday. → He talked angrily to his brother yesterday.
translate: वह गुस्से से अपने कमरे में चला गया। → He angrily went into his room.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about someone who spoke angrily.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'in a way that shows strong annoyance or fury'?
usage_tip: 'Replied angrily' is common in stories.

simple_explanation: In a joyful, pleased way. When you do something happily, you feel joy or pleasure while doing it, and it usually shows.
example_1: The children played happily in the park.
example_2: She happily accepted the job offer.
example_3: They lived happily in the countryside for years.
collocations: happily married, live happily, happily accept, happily surprised
grammar_pattern: verb + happily (They danced happily)
common_mistake: She is happily today because of the good news.
correct_version: She is happy today because of the good news.
why_it_s_wrong: After 'is', use the adjective 'happy', not the adverb.
pronunciation_tip: Three syllables: HAP-uh-lee - stress on the first syllable.
spelling_tip: "Happy" changes "y" to "i" before adding "-ly": happy -> happily.
etymology: From Old Norse "happ" (luck, chance) via "happy" (originally "lucky," later "joyful") + "-ly."
prefix_root_suffix: happy = root (lucky, joyful) + -ly = adverb suffix (y -> i before -ly)
mnemonic: HAPPILY - picture someone HAPPILY skipping down the street, smiling.
memory_trick: HAPPY → HAPPILY: Y becomes I.
visual_association: A child laughing while running through falling autumn leaves.
difference_explained: Happy = adjective (she is happy). Happily = adverb (she sang happily).
mini_conversation:
A: How did she react when you told her?
B: She happily hugged everyone in the room.
everyday_scene: Everyday: A narrator closes the story with, "And so, they lived happily for many years after that."
news_style_line: News-style: "Families gathered happily at the reopening of the community park."
casual_conversation: Casual: "I'd happily help you move this weekend if you need it."
mcq_options: A) In a joyful, pleased way  B) In a sad, upset way  C) In an angry way  D) In a nervous way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The dog wagged its tail ______ when its owner came home. → happily
find_and_fix_to_correct: They married happily last summer in a small ceremony but not since. → They got married happily last summer in a small ceremony.
translate: बच्चे पार्क में खुशी से खेल रहे थे। → The children were playing happily in the park.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something you do happily.
