write_your_own_sentence: Write about something that happens every time you go out.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'on each occasion that'?
usage_tip: 'Every time' is always two words.

simple_explanation: With the purpose of.
example_1: She studied in order to pass.
example_2: I study hard in order to pass.
example_3: We left early in order to avoid traffic.
collocations: in order to, succeed, in order for
grammar_pattern: in order to + base verb
common_mistake: She studied in order pass.
correct_version: She studied in order to pass.
why_it_s_wrong: 'In order' always needs 'to' + verb after it.
etymology: in + order + to.
mnemonic: 'Taaki' = in order to.
memory_trick: 'In order to' always keeps its 'to' — three words, one purpose.
visual_association: A target with an arrow.
difference_explained: Same meaning. 'To' alone is shorter and more common in speech.
related_words: to, so as to, so that
mini_conversation: A: Why do you run every day? / B: In order to stay fit.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Save money in order to travel.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Roads were closed in order to allow the parade.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I'm cutting sugar in order to lose weight.'
mcq_question: Choose: She woke up early in order ___ the train.

find_and_fix_to_correct: I came here for to meet you. → I came here to meet you. / I came here in order to meet you.

write_your_own_sentence: Write about something you do in order to stay healthy.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review

simple_explanation: With the purpose of, formal.
example_1: He left early so as to avoid traffic.
example_2: He left early so as to avoid traffic.
example_3: Speak slowly so as to be clear.
collocations: so as to avoid, so as not to
grammar_pattern: so as to + base verb
common_mistake: He left early so as avoid traffic.
correct_version: He left early so as to avoid traffic.
why_it_s_wrong: 'So as' always needs 'to' + verb after it.
etymology: so + as + to.
mnemonic: 'Taaki' (formal) = so as to.
memory_trick: 'So as to' is a formal, slightly old-fashioned way to say 'in order to'.
visual_association: An arrow hitting a target.
confusing_word: so as to vs so that
difference_explained: So as to + verb (so as to win). So that + clause (so that we win).
related_words: in order to, to, so that
mini_conversation: A: Why did you whisper? / B: So as not to wake the baby.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'We locked the gate so as to keep the dog in.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Trains were cancelled so as to ensure safety.'
casual_conversation: Casual: (too formal — just say 'to')
mcq_question: Choose: She wrote it down so as ___ forget.
mcq_options: A) not to  B) to not  C) don't  D) not
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He left early ___ ___ ___ avoid traffic. → so as to
find_and_fix_to_correct: He left early so as he could catch the bus. → He left early so as to catch the bus.
translate: ट्रैफ़िक से बचने के लिए वह जल्दी निकला। → He left early so as to avoid traffic.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a formal sentence using 'so as to'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'with the purpose of, formal'?
usage_tip: The negative is 'so as not to', not 'so as to not' (in formal writing).

simple_explanation: Used to show a comparison.

example_2: Compared to last year, prices are high.
example_3: My room is small compared to yours.

grammar_pattern: compared to + noun, + clause
common_mistake: Compare to last year, sales are up.
correct_version: Compared to last year, sales are up.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Compare' must be 'compared' in this phrase.
etymology: compare + -d + to.
mnemonic: 'Ke muqable' = compared to.
memory_trick: 'Compared to' sets up a comparison — remember the '-d' ending on 'compared'.
visual_association: Two bars on a chart.
difference_explained: Compared to + noun (compared to Delhi). Than after a comparative (bigger than Delhi).
related_words: than, next to, in comparison with
mini_conversation: A: Is Pune cold? / B: Compared to Delhi, not really.

news_style_line: News-style: 'Sales rose 10% compared to last year.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'This is nothing compared to my mom's cooking!'
mcq_question: Choose: ___ to Mumbai, Pune is quieter.
mcq_options: A) Compare  B) Compared  C) Comparing  D) Comparison
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___ last year, sales are up. → Compared to
find_and_fix_to_correct: My house is bigger compared to yours. → My house is bigger than yours. / My house is big compared to yours.
translate: पिछले साल के मुकाबले दाम ज़्यादा हैं। → Compared to last year, prices are high.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a comparison using 'compared to'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to show a comparison'?
usage_tip: Don't use 'compared to' with a comparative (bigger); use 'than'.

simple_explanation: Equally as.
example_1: She is just as smart as her sister.
example_2: She is just as smart as her brother.
example_3: Just as I left, it started raining.
collocations: just as good, just as important, just as well
grammar_pattern: subject + be + just as + adjective + as + noun
common_mistake: She is just as smart than her sister (wrong word).
correct_version: She is just as smart as her sister.
why_it_s_wrong: 'As … as' is a pair — the second word is 'as', not 'than'.
etymology: just + as.
mnemonic: 'Utna hi' = just as.
memory_trick: 'Just as...as' adds extra emphasis to an equal comparison.
visual_association: Two equal glasses.
difference_explained: Just as = exactly equal (stronger). As … as = equal. 'Just as' also means 'at the same moment'.
mini_conversation: A: Is the new phone better? / B: It's just as good as the old one.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Just as I sat down, the bell rang.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The second half was just as exciting.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'You're just as bad as me!'
mcq_question: Choose: This road is just as busy ___ that one.
mcq_options: A) than  B) as  C) like  D) so
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She is ___ ___ smart as her sister. → just as
find_and_fix_to_correct: Rice is just as healthy than roti. → Rice is just as healthy as roti.
translate: वह अपनी बहन जितनी ही होशियार है। → She is just as smart as her sister.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence with 'just as … as'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'equally as'?
usage_tip: 'Just as I…' = at the exact moment when I…

simple_explanation: Shows two things are equal.
example_1: She is as tall as her brother.
example_2: She is as tall as her brother.
example_3: It's not as hot as yesterday.
collocations: as tall as, as good as, as soon as
grammar_pattern: subject + be + as + adjective + as + noun
word_forms: as + adjective + as · not as + adjective + as
common_mistake: She is as tall than her brother.
correct_version: She is as tall as her brother.
why_it_s_wrong: The pattern is 'as … as' — never 'as … than'.
spelling_tip: AS … AS: the same word twice.
etymology: as + adjective + as.
mnemonic: 'Utna hi … jitna' = as … as.
memory_trick: 'As...as' wraps around an adjective to show two things are exactly equal.
visual_association: Two children of the same height.
difference_explained: As … as = equal. Comparative + than = not equal (taller than).
mini_conversation: A: Is the new flat big? / B: Not as big as our old one.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Come as soon as you can.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'This winter is not as cold as last year.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'You're as stubborn as a mule!'
mcq_question: Choose: My bag is as heavy ___ yours.
mcq_options: A) than  B) as  C) like  D) to
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She is ___ tall ___ her brother. → as...as
find_and_fix_to_correct: He is not so tall like me. → He is not as tall as me.
translate: वह अपने भाई जितनी लंबी है। → She is as tall as her brother.
write_your_own_sentence: Write three comparisons with 'as … as' and 'not as … as'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'shows two things are equal'?
usage_tip: 'As soon as possible', 'as much as you like' — common fixed uses.

simple_explanation: Used to explain or correct what you said.
example_1: I mean, it's not that bad.
example_2: I mean, it's not that bad.
example_3: He's nice — I mean, he's a bit loud, but nice.
collocations: I mean, it's, I mean to say
grammar_pattern: I mean, + clause (clarification)
common_mistake: I mean to say, it's not bad.
correct_version: I mean, it's not bad.
why_it_s_wrong: 'I mean' already means 'what I want to say is', so 'to say' is extra.
etymology: I + mean.
mnemonic: 'Matlab' = I mean.
memory_trick: 'I mean' rewinds and clarifies exactly what you're trying to say.
visual_association: A person rewording with hand gestures.
synonyms: that is, what I'm saying is
difference_explained: I mean = I'm explaining or correcting. You know = I'm checking you follow.
related_words: that is, in other words, you know
mini_conversation: A: Did you like the film? / B: It was okay. I mean, the songs were good.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'We're late — I mean, a little late.'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I mean, seriously? Who does that?'
mcq_question: Choose: 'It's cheap. ___, it's not expensive for what you get.'
mcq_options: A) I mean  B) I means  C) Mean I  D) I meant to
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___, it's not that bad. → I mean
find_and_fix_to_correct: I mean to say that I am mean to say sorry. → I mean, I'm sorry. / I want to say sorry.
translate: मेरा मतलब, यह इतना बुरा नहीं है। → I mean, it's not that bad.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence where you correct yourself with 'I mean'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to explain or correct what you said'?
usage_tip: Too many 'I mean's make you sound unsure — use it sometimes, not every sentence.

simple_explanation: Used to check understanding, or as a filler.
example_2: It's, you know, complicated.
example_3: You know the shop near the bank? It's closed.
collocations: you know, what, you know, like
where_it_s_used: Filling pauses, checking the listener follows
grammar_pattern: clause, you know, clause (filler/check)
common_mistake: You know na, it's complicated.
correct_version: You know, it's complicated.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Na' is Hindi; 'you know' already asks the listener to agree.
spelling_tip: YOU KNOW: two words. Silent K.
etymology: you + know.
mnemonic: 'Pata hai na?' = you know.
memory_trick: 'You know' is a filler that checks the listener is following along.
visual_association: Two friends nodding.
difference_explained: You know = checking the listener follows. I mean = explaining yourself.
mini_conversation: A: Where do you live? / B: You know the big temple? Near there.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'You know what? Let's order pizza.'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'It was, you know, a bit awkward.'
mcq_question: Choose: '___ that café on MG Road? Let's meet there.'
mcq_options: A) You know  B) You knows  C) Know you  D) You known
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: It's, ___ ___, complicated. → you know
find_and_fix_to_correct: It is, you knowing, complicated. → It's, you know, complicated.
translate: तुम्हें पता है, यह थोड़ा मुश्किल है। → It's, you know, a bit difficult.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence starting with 'You know the…?'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to check understanding, or as a filler'?
usage_tip: In interviews, avoid saying 'you know' again and again — it can sound unprepared.

simple_explanation: To be annoyed by something; to be careful about something.
example_1: Do you mind if I sit here?
example_2: I don't mind waiting.
example_3: Mind the gap!
collocations: don't mind, would you mind, mind your language
action_sequence: Before: someone asks for a favour → During: you think about it → After: say 'I don't mind'
grammar_pattern: mind + -ing / Do you mind if … ? / Would you mind + -ing?
common_mistake: Would you mind to close the door?
correct_version: Would you mind closing the door?
why_it_s_wrong: After 'mind', use the -ing form, not 'to' + verb.
etymology: Old English 'gemynd' (memory).
mnemonic: 'Mind' = बुरा मानना — 'Do you mind?' = आपको बुरा तो नहीं लगेगा?
memory_trick: MIND + -ING, always.
visual_association: A person politely asking to open a window.
difference_explained: 'I don't mind' = it's okay with me. 'I don't care' = it's not important to me (can sound rude).
mini_conversation: A: Do you mind if I open the window? / B: Not at all, go ahead.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I don't mind spicy food.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Passengers were asked to mind their belongings.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Mind your own business!'
mcq_question: Choose: Would you mind ___ me the salt?
mcq_options: A) to pass  B) passing  C) pass  D) passed
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Do you ___ if I use your pen? → mind
find_and_fix_to_correct: Do you mind if I will sit here? → Do you mind if I sit here?
translate: क्या आपको बुरा लगेगा अगर मैं यहाँ बैठूँ? → Do you mind if I sit here?
write_your_own_sentence: Write a polite request with 'Would you mind…?'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to be annoyed by something; to be careful about something'?
usage_tip: To say yes to 'Do you mind…?', answer 'No, not at all' — because you don't mind.

simple_explanation: To not like something or someone.
example_2: She dislikes waking up early.
example_3: Many kids dislike vegetables.
collocations: strongly dislike, likes and dislikes
action_sequence: Before: try something → During: don't enjoy it → After: avoid it next time
grammar_pattern: dislike + noun / dislike + -ing
common_mistake: I am disliking this food.
correct_version: I dislike this food. / I don't like this food.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Dislike' is a state verb, so no -ing.
etymology: dis (not) + like.
mnemonic: 'Dislike' = नापसंद।
memory_trick: DIS- flips the meaning: like → dislike.
visual_association: A child pushing away a plate.
difference_explained: Dislike = not like (mild). Hate = very strong.
mini_conversation: A: Is there any food you dislike? / B: Bitter gourd!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I dislike crowded buses.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Many voters dislike both parties.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I don't hate it, I just dislike it.'
mcq_question: Choose: She dislikes ___ in the rain.
mcq_options: A) to walk  B) walking  C) walk  D) walked
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Tell me your likes and ___. → dislikes
find_and_fix_to_correct: I am disliking him. → I dislike him. / I don't like him.
translate: मुझे शोर पसंद नहीं। → I dislike noise.
write_your_own_sentence: Write three things you dislike.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to not like something or someone'?
usage_tip: In speech, 'I don't like' is more common than 'I dislike'.

simple_explanation: To get something useful, or to get more of something.
example_1: I gained experience at my first job.
example_2: He has gained weight.
example_3: You have nothing to lose and everything to gain.
collocations: gain weight, gain experience, gain confidence
action_sequence: Before: start the work → During: learn a lot → After: now you have experience
grammar_pattern: gain + noun
common_mistake: I gained a lot of knowledges.
correct_version: I gained a lot of knowledge.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Knowledge' is uncountable — no -s.
etymology: Old French 'gaaignier' (to earn).
mnemonic: 'Gain' = हासिल करना — weight gain = वज़न बढ़ना।
memory_trick: GAIN is the opposite of LOSE.
visual_association: A plant growing taller.
difference_explained: Gain = get something (skills, weight). Earn = get money by working.
mini_conversation: A: What did you learn from the internship? / B: I gained a lot of confidence.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I gained 3 kg during the holidays!'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The rupee gained against the dollar today.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'No pain, no gain!'
mcq_question: Choose: He ___ weight after the surgery.
mcq_options: A) gained  B) earned  C) won  D) got up
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She wants to ___ more experience in teaching. → gain
find_and_fix_to_correct: I gained money from my job. → I earned money from my job.
translate: मैंने बहुत अनुभव हासिल किया। → I gained a lot of experience.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a skill you gained this year.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to get something useful, or to get more of something'?
usage_tip: 'No pain, no gain' = you must work hard to get results.

simple_explanation: To go up by itself; to increase.
example_1: The sun rises in the east.
example_2: Prices are rising.
example_3: The river rose after the rain.
collocations: prices rise, the sun rises, rise sharply
action_sequence: Before: the day starts → During: the sun comes up → After: it's morning
grammar_pattern: subject + rise (no object)
common_mistake: The government rose the prices.
correct_version: The government raised the prices.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Rise' has no object — things rise by themselves. To make something go up, use 'raise'.
spelling_tip: R-I-S-E. Past: ROSE. Past participle: RISEN.
etymology: Old English 'rīsan'.
mnemonic: SUNRISE — सूरज अपने आप 'उठता' है।
memory_trick: RISE → ROSE → RISEN, like DRIVE → DROVE → DRIVEN.
visual_association: The sun coming up over hills.
difference_explained: Rise = goes up by itself (no object). Raise = you lift something (with object).
mini_conversation: A: Why is petrol so costly? / B: Oil prices have risen again.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'The dough will rise in an hour.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Temperatures will rise by 2°C this week.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Rise and shine!' (= wake up)
mcq_question: Choose: The sun ___ at 6 a.m. today.
mcq_options: A) raised  B) rose  C) rised  D) risen
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Prices have ___ a lot this year. → risen
find_and_fix_to_correct: The prices are raising. → The prices are rising.
translate: कीमतें बढ़ रही हैं। → Prices are rising.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence about something that rose recently.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to go up by itself; to increase'?
usage_tip: 'Rise' has no object: 'Prices rose', never 'rose the prices'.

simple_explanation: To lift something up; to increase something; to bring up children.
example_1: Raise your hand if you know.
example_2: They raised the fees.
example_3: She raised three children alone.
collocations: raise your hand, raise money, raise a question
action_sequence: Before: have a question → During: raise your hand → After: the teacher calls you
grammar_pattern: raise + object
common_mistake: Please rise your hand.
correct_version: Please raise your hand.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Raise' needs an object (your hand). 'Rise' does not.
etymology: Old Norse 'reisa'.
mnemonic: 'Raise' = हाथ 'उठाओ'।
memory_trick: RAISE something. It RISES by itself.
visual_association: A student raising a hand.
difference_explained: Raise + object (raise your hand). Rise alone (the sun rises).
mini_conversation: A: Any questions? / B: (raising hand) Yes, one.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Please raise your hand before speaking.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The bank raised interest rates.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'She raised a good point.'
mcq_question: Choose: If you agree, ___ your hand.
mcq_options: A) rise  B) raise  C) rose  D) risen
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The school ___ money for the flood victims. → raised
find_and_fix_to_correct: He was rised by his grandparents. → He was raised by his grandparents.
translate: अपना हाथ उठाओ। → Raise your hand.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a time you raised a question in class.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to lift something up; to increase something; to bring up children'?
usage_tip: 'Raise' also means bring up children: 'I was raised in Lucknow.'

simple_explanation: To happen because of something ('result from'), or to cause something ('result in').
example_2: The accident resulted from speeding.
example_3: His hard work resulted in success.
collocations: result in, result from, as a result
action_sequence: Before: something happens → During: it has an effect → After: the result follows
grammar_pattern: A + result in + B (effect) / B + result from + A (cause)
common_mistake: The rain resulted into floods.
correct_version: The rain resulted in floods.
why_it_s_wrong: The phrase is 'result IN' (effect) or 'result FROM' (cause) — not 'into'.
pronunciation_tip: Stress on ZULT: 'ri-ZULT'. The S sounds like Z.
etymology: Latin 'resultare' (to spring back).
mnemonic: Exam RESULT — मेहनत का परिणाम।
memory_trick: Result IN = the effect. Result FROM = the cause.
visual_association: Dominoes falling one after another.
difference_explained: Result in = causes (rain → floods). Result from = is caused by (floods ← rain).
mini_conversation: A: Why was the match stopped? / B: The storm resulted in a power cut.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Skipping breakfast can result in headaches.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The collision resulted in three injuries.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'As a result, I missed the bus!'
mcq_question: Choose: Smoking can result ___ serious illness.
mcq_options: A) into  B) in  C) from  D) to
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Careless driving often ___ in accidents. → results
find_and_fix_to_correct: The fire resulted by a short circuit. → The fire resulted from a short circuit.
translate: बारिश से बाढ़ आ गई। → The rain resulted in floods.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a cause and effect sentence with 'result in'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to happen because of something ('result from'), or to cause something ('result in')'?
usage_tip: 'As a result' starts a sentence that gives the effect.

simple_explanation: To become part of a group; to connect things.
example_2: She joined the company in 2022.
example_3: Join the two wires.
collocations: join a club, join the team, join us
action_sequence: Before: hear about the group → During: sign up → After: become a member
grammar_pattern: join + group/person (no preposition)
common_mistake: He joined in our company last year.
correct_version: He joined our company last year.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Join' takes the group directly — no 'in' or 'with'.
etymology: Old French 'joindre'.
mnemonic: 'Joining date' — नौकरी में 'जुड़ने' की तारीख।
memory_trick: JOIN + group, no 'in'.
visual_association: People adding hands in a team huddle.
difference_explained: Join = become part of a group. Join in = take part in an activity already happening.
mini_conversation: A: We're going for lunch. / B: Can I join you?
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Join us for dinner on Sunday.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Five new members joined the board.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Come on, join in the game!'
mcq_question: Choose: She ___ the dance class last month.
mcq_options: A) joined in  B) joined  C) joined with  D) joins to
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Would you like to ___ our team? → join
find_and_fix_to_correct: I will join in the office on Monday. → I will join the office on Monday.
translate: मैंने नई कंपनी जॉइन की। → I joined a new company.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a group or club you joined.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to become part of a group; to connect things'?
usage_tip: 'Joining date' is Indian English; 'start date' is common abroad.

simple_explanation: To go to see a person or a place.
example_2: Have you visited Agra?
example_3: Visit our website for details.
collocations: visit a friend, visit a place, visit a doctor
action_sequence: Before: plan a trip → During: go and see the place → After: come back home
grammar_pattern: visit + person/place
common_mistake: I visited to Jaipur last year.
correct_version: I visited Jaipur last year.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Visit' takes the place directly — no 'to'.
etymology: Latin 'visitare' (to go to see).
mnemonic: Visiting card — मिलने पर देने वाला कार्ड।
memory_trick: VISIT + place, no TO.
visual_association: A family at a monument.
difference_explained: Visit = go to a person's place or a place. Meet = see someone anywhere.
mini_conversation: A: What did you do in the holidays? / B: We visited Kerala.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Visit the doctor if the fever continues.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The PM will visit Japan next month.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Come visit us sometime!'
mcq_question: Choose: I want to ___ Ladakh one day.
mcq_options: A) visit to  B) visit  C) visiting to  D) visit in
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: My cousins ___ us every Diwali. → visit
find_and_fix_to_correct: We visited to the museum. → We visited the museum.
translate: हम ताजमहल घूमने गए। → We visited the Taj Mahal.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a place you visited.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to go to see a person or a place'?
usage_tip: 'Pay a visit' = visit: 'Let's pay Grandma a visit.'

simple_explanation: To put something over something else; to include a topic.
example_2: The book covers all topics.
example_3: Snow covered the hills.
collocations: cover your mouth, cover the cost, cover a topic
action_sequence: Before: see the open dish → During: put a lid on → After: it's covered
grammar_pattern: cover + thing (+ with + thing)
common_mistake: Cover the food by a plate.
correct_version: Cover the food with a plate.
why_it_s_wrong: You cover something WITH something.
etymology: Old French 'covrir'.
mnemonic: Phone COVER — फ़ोन को 'ढकने' वाला।
memory_trick: COVER WITH, not 'by'.
visual_association: A lid on a pot.
difference_explained: Cover = put something over. Hide = keep out of sight.
mini_conversation: A: Did the lecture cover chapter 5? / B: Yes, all of it.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Cover your mouth when you cough.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Insurance will cover the repair cost.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Don't worry, I've got you covered.'
mcq_question: Choose: Cover the plants ___ a sheet.
mcq_options: A) by  B) with  C) from  D) at
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Please ___ the milk, or flies will get in. → cover
find_and_fix_to_correct: The table was covered by a cloth. → The table was covered with a cloth.
translate: खाना ढक दो। → Cover the food.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about something you cover every day.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to put something over something else; to include a topic'?
usage_tip: 'Cover for someone' = do their work while they're away.

simple_explanation: To make something full.
example_2: Please fill in this form.
example_3: The room filled with smoke.
collocations: fill a glass, fill in a form, fill up
related_phrasal_verbs: fill in, fill out, fill up
action_sequence: Before: take the empty bottle → During: pour the water → After: it's full
grammar_pattern: fill + thing + with + thing
common_mistake: Fill water in the bottle.
correct_version: Fill the bottle with water.
why_it_s_wrong: You fill the container WITH the thing.
etymology: Old English 'fyllan'.
mnemonic: Pen REFILL — पेन में फिर से स्याही भरना।
memory_trick: FILL → FULL.
visual_association: A glass being filled.
difference_explained: Both mean complete a form. 'Fill in' (UK) also means fill a blank.
mini_conversation: A: Where do I apply? / B: Just fill in this form.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Fill the tank before the trip.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The stadium was filled with fans.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Fill me in — what happened?' (= tell me)

write_your_own_sentence: Write your aim for the next year.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'to try or plan to achieve something; to point at a target'?

memory_trick: LOOK AT = eyes on it. SEE = it just comes into your eyes.

confusing_word: look at vs see vs watch

memory_trick: GET ON the bus, GET OFF the bus.

example_3: At last I understand!
collocations: at last, finally
grammar_pattern: At last, + clause / clause + at last
common_mistake: At the last, we won.
correct_version: At last, we won.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At last' has no 'the'. ('At the last minute' is a different phrase.)
etymology: at + last.
mnemonic: 'Aakhirkaar' = at last.
memory_trick: AT LAST = sigh of relief.
visual_association: A runner crossing a finish line.
difference_explained: At last = finally. At least = minimum.
mini_conversation: A: The results are out! / B: At last!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'At last, the rain has stopped.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'At last, the new bridge has opened.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Friday at last!'
mcq_question: Choose: After three hours, the train arrived ___.
mcq_options: A) at least  B) at last  C) lastly  D) last
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: We found the keys ___ ___. → at last
find_and_fix_to_correct: At the last I got the job. → At last, I got the job.

reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'finally, after a long time'?
usage_tip: 'At last' shows relief; 'finally' can be neutral.

simple_explanation: Until now.
example_2: How's the new job so far?
example_3: I have read three chapters so far.
collocations: so far, so good
grammar_pattern: So far, + present perfect
common_mistake: So far I did two tasks.
correct_version: So far I have done two tasks.
why_it_s_wrong: 'So far' goes with the present perfect (have done).
etymology: so + far.
mnemonic: 'Ab tak' = so far.
memory_trick: SO FAR + HAVE DONE.
visual_association: A progress bar at 60%.
difference_explained: So far = until now (positive sentences). Yet = until now (questions, negatives).
related_words: until now, up to now, yet
mini_conversation: A: How's the course? / B: So far, so good.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I've saved ₹5,000 so far.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'So far, no one has been arrested.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'So far, I love it!'
mcq_question: Choose: I ___ three emails so far.
mcq_options: A) send  B) have sent  C) sent  D) am sending
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: How is the trip ___ ___? → so far
find_and_fix_to_correct: So far I finished two books. → So far, I have finished two books.
translate: अब तक सब ठीक है। → So far, so good.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about your progress this year using 'so far'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'until now'?
usage_tip: 'So far, so good' = everything is fine until now.

simple_explanation: At this exact moment; immediately.
example_2: Call him right now!
example_3: Right now, I'm reading a book.
collocations: right now, not right now
grammar_pattern: right now + present continuous
common_mistake: I am busy just now right now.
correct_version: I am busy right now.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Just now' and 'right now' — use one.
etymology: right + now.
mnemonic: 'Abhi' = right now.
memory_trick: RIGHT NOW = this second.
visual_association: A clock with a red dot.
difference_explained: Right now = at this moment. Just now = a moment ago.
mini_conversation: A: Can we talk? / B: Not right now, I'm driving.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I need water right now!'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Right now, the focus is on rescue work.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Come here right now!'
mcq_question: Choose: I'm cooking ___. Can I call you back?
mcq_options: A) just now  B) right now  C) now right  D) yet
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She's in a meeting ___ ___. → right now
find_and_fix_to_correct: I will do it just now. (meaning 'immediately') → I will do it right now.
translate: मैं अभी व्यस्त हूँ। → I'm busy right now.
write_your_own_sentence: Write what you are doing right now.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at this exact moment; immediately'?
usage_tip: In Indian English 'just now' can mean 'soon'; abroad it means 'a moment ago'.

simple_explanation: Used in negatives and questions to make them stronger.
example_1: I don't like it at all.
example_2: Did you sleep at all?
example_3: Not at all!
collocations: not at all, at all
grammar_pattern: not … at all / Did you … at all?
common_mistake: I don't like at all it.
correct_version: I don't like it at all.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At all' goes at the end of the negative.
etymology: at + all.
word_family: all, at all, not at all
mnemonic: 'Bilkul bhi nahi' = not at all.
memory_trick: NOT … AT ALL = zero.
visual_association: A meter at zero.
confusing_word: at all vs not at all
difference_explained: 'At all' strengthens a negative. 'Not at all' alone = 'You're welcome' or 'No, not even a little'.
related_words: whatsoever, a bit, in the least
mini_conversation: A: Do you mind if I sit here? / B: Not at all.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I didn't understand the lesson at all.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Some villages got no help at all.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I'm not tired at all!'
mcq_options: A) at all  B) all at  C) at least  D) at last
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She didn't eat anything ___ ___. → at all
find_and_fix_to_correct: I am not at all agree. → I don't agree at all.
translate: मुझे यह बिल्कुल पसंद नहीं। → I don't like it at all.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence with 'not … at all'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used in negatives and questions to make them stronger'?
usage_tip: 'Not at all' is a polite reply to 'Thank you' or 'Do you mind?'.

simple_explanation: Used to give a reason ('remember that…'), or to say something happened despite a plan.
example_1: Don't be angry — he's only a child, after all.
example_2: It didn't rain after all.
example_3: After all, it's your decision.
collocations: after all, after all this time
grammar_pattern: …, after all. / After all, + reason
common_mistake: After all I will come, I decided.
correct_version: I decided to come after all.
why_it_s_wrong: 'After all' (= in the end, despite the plan) usually goes at the end.
etymology: after + all.
mnemonic: 'Aakhir' (reason) = after all.
memory_trick: AFTER ALL = remember this reason.
visual_association: A person shrugging with a smile.
difference_explained: After all = despite what was planned, or 'remember'. At last = finally, after waiting.
mini_conversation: A: You said you weren't coming! / B: I changed my mind — I came after all.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Let him sleep. He's tired, after all.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The match went ahead after all.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'After all, we're family!'
mcq_question: Choose: I thought I'd fail, but I passed ___.
mcq_options: A) after all  B) at all  C) at last all  D) all after
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: We didn't need the umbrella ___ ___. → after all
find_and_fix_to_correct: At last it didn't rain. (meaning 'contrary to the plan') → It didn't rain after all.
translate: आख़िर वह बच्चा ही तो है। → He's only a child, after all.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence using 'after all' to give a reason.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to give a reason ('remember that…'), or to say something happened despite a plan'?
usage_tip: 'After all' does NOT mean 'finally' — use 'at last' or 'finally' for that.

simple_explanation: Usually; in most cases.
example_1: In general, I like my job.
example_2: People in general are kind.
example_3: In general, prices are high in Mumbai.
collocations: in general, generally speaking
grammar_pattern: In general, + clause / noun + in general
common_mistake: In generally, it's fine.
correct_version: In general, it's fine. / Generally, it's fine.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'in general' or 'generally' — not a mix.
etymology: in + general.
mnemonic: 'Aam taur par' = in general.
memory_trick: IN GENERAL = GENERALLY.
visual_association: A big crowd seen from above.
difference_explained: Same meaning. 'In general' can also follow a noun: 'people in general'.
mini_conversation: A: Do you like the city? / B: In general, yes, but not the traffic.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Kids in general love cartoons.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'In general, the monsoon was normal this year.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I'm a morning person in general.'
mcq_question: Choose: ___, I agree with your plan.
mcq_options: A) In generally  B) In general  C) General  D) On general
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___, the food here is good. → In general
find_and_fix_to_correct: On general, I sleep early. → In general, I sleep early.
translate: आमतौर पर मुझे अपना काम पसंद है। → In general, I like my job.
write_your_own_sentence: Write something that is true 'in general' about your city.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'usually; in most cases'?
usage_tip: 'In general' is opposite to 'in particular' (for one thing).

simple_explanation: At the correct time; not late.
example_2: Please submit it on time.
example_3: She is always on time.
collocations: on time, right on time, arrive on time
grammar_pattern: be/arrive + on time
common_mistake: He came in time to the meeting. (meaning 'at 10 exactly')
correct_version: He came to the meeting on time.
why_it_s_wrong: 'On time' = at the planned time. 'In time' = early enough.
etymology: on + time.
mnemonic: 'Samay par' = on time.
memory_trick: ON TIME = on the dot.
visual_association: A clock at 9:00 and a person arriving.
difference_explained: On time = at the planned time. In time = before it's too late.
mini_conversation: A: Was the flight late? / B: No, right on time.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Pay your bills on time.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Only 60% of trains ran on time.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Wow, you're on time for once!'
mcq_options: A) on time  B) in the time  C) at time  D) by time
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Please reach ___ ___ for the exam. → on time
find_and_fix_to_correct: He always comes at time. → He always comes on time.
translate: ट्रेन समय पर थी। → The train was on time.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about someone who is always on time.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at the correct time; not late'?
usage_tip: 'Punctual' is the adjective for a person who is always on time.

simple_explanation: Now; at this time.
example_1: He's not here at the moment.
example_2: At the moment, I'm working from home.
example_3: I'm busy at the moment.
collocations: at the moment, for the moment
grammar_pattern: at the moment + present continuous
common_mistake: At this moment of time, he is busy.
correct_version: At the moment, he is busy.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At this moment of time' is wordy; say 'at the moment'.
etymology: at + the + moment.
mnemonic: 'Is waqt' = at the moment.
memory_trick: AT THE MOMENT = NOW (a bit formal).
visual_association: A 'Busy' light on an office door.
confusing_word: at the moment vs right now
difference_explained: Same meaning. 'At the moment' is a bit more polite on the phone.
mini_conversation: A: Can I speak to Mr Rao? / B: He's in a meeting at the moment.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I'm reading a good book at the moment.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'At the moment, there is no plan to close schools.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I'm broke at the moment!'
mcq_question: Choose: I'm living with my cousin ___.
mcq_options: A) in the moment  B) at the moment  C) at moment  D) on the moment
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Sorry, she isn't available ___ ___ ___. → at the moment
find_and_fix_to_correct: At this point of time I am free. → At the moment, I'm free.
translate: वह इस समय यहाँ नहीं है। → He is not here at the moment.
write_your_own_sentence: Write three things you are doing at the moment.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'now; at this time'?
usage_tip: On the phone: 'I'm afraid he's not available at the moment.'

simple_explanation: Finally, after a long time or many changes.
example_1: In the end, we took a taxi.
example_2: In the end, everything was fine.
example_3: We argued, but in the end we agreed.
collocations: in the end
grammar_pattern: In the end, + clause
common_mistake: At the end we took a taxi. (meaning 'finally')
correct_version: In the end, we took a taxi.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At the end' needs 'of' (at the end of the film). For 'finally', use 'in the end'.
etymology: in + the + end.
mnemonic: 'Aakhir mein' = in the end.
memory_trick: IN THE END = finally. AT THE END OF = the last part of something.
visual_association: The last page of a storybook.
confusing_word: in the end vs at the end
difference_explained: In the end = finally. At the end of = the last part (at the end of the day).
mini_conversation: A: Did you buy the red phone or the black one? / B: In the end, the black one.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'In the end, it's your choice.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'In the end, the team lost by one goal.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'It all worked out in the end!'
mcq_question: Choose: We waited for hours, but ___ we went home.
mcq_options: A) at the end  B) in the end  C) in end  D) on the end
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___ ___, everyone was happy. → In the end
find_and_fix_to_correct: At the end, I chose science. → In the end, I chose science.
translate: आख़िर में हमने टैक्सी ली। → In the end, we took a taxi.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a short story ending with 'In the end…'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'finally, after a long time or many changes'?
usage_tip: 'At the end of the day' = when everything is considered.

simple_explanation: Not on purpose; accidentally.
example_1: I took your pen by mistake.
example_2: Sorry, I sent it to you by mistake.
example_3: He deleted the file by mistake.
collocations: by mistake, send by mistake
grammar_pattern: verb + by mistake
common_mistake: I did it from mistake.
correct_version: I did it by mistake.
why_it_s_wrong: The phrase is 'BY mistake'.
etymology: by + mistake.
mnemonic: 'Galti se' = by mistake.
memory_trick: BY MISTAKE = not on purpose.
visual_association: A person holding the wrong umbrella.
difference_explained: By mistake = without meaning to. On purpose = meaning to.
mini_conversation: A: Is this my bag? / B: Oh sorry, I took it by mistake!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I pressed the wrong button by mistake.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Money was sent to the wrong account by mistake.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Oops, I ate your chocolate by mistake!'
mcq_question: Choose: I called my boss ___ mistake.
mcq_options: A) from  B) by  C) with  D) in
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Sorry, I sat in your seat ___ ___. → by mistake
find_and_fix_to_correct: I did a mistake by mistake. → I did it by mistake. / I made a mistake.
translate: गलती से मैंने तुम्हारा पेन ले लिया। → I took your pen by mistake.
write_your_own_sentence: Write an apology using 'by mistake'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'not on purpose; accidentally'?
usage_tip: 'By accident' means the same.

simple_explanation: Deliberately; because you wanted to.
example_1: Did you do that on purpose?
example_2: He broke it on purpose.
example_3: I left early on purpose.
collocations: on purpose, did it on purpose
grammar_pattern: verb + on purpose
common_mistake: He did it with purpose.
correct_version: He did it on purpose.
why_it_s_wrong: The phrase is 'ON purpose'.
etymology: on + purpose.
mnemonic: 'Jaan-boojhkar' = on purpose.
memory_trick: ON PURPOSE = I planned it.
visual_association: A child smiling after spilling milk.
difference_explained: On purpose = meant to. By mistake = didn't mean to.
mini_conversation: A: You stepped on my foot! / B: Sorry, not on purpose!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'I left the door open on purpose — for the cat.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Police believe the fire was started on purpose.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'You're annoying me on purpose!'
mcq_question: Choose: I didn't break it ___ purpose, I promise.
mcq_options: A) by  B) on  C) for  D) with
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: She ignored me ___ ___. → on purpose
find_and_fix_to_correct: He did it by purpose. → He did it on purpose.
translate: उसने जानबूझकर ऐसा किया। → He did it on purpose.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a sentence with 'on purpose' and one with 'by mistake'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'deliberately; because you wanted to'?
usage_tip: 'Not on purpose!' = I didn't mean to — sorry.

simple_explanation: Before anything else; used to start a list of points.
example_1: First of all, thank you for coming.
example_2: First of all, switch off the gas.
example_3: First of all, let me introduce myself.
collocations: first of all, then, finally
grammar_pattern: First of all, + clause
common_mistake: First of all, firstly I want to thank you.
correct_version: First of all, I want to thank you.
why_it_s_wrong: 'First of all' and 'firstly' mean the same — use one.
etymology: first + of + all.
mnemonic: 'Sabse pehle' = first of all.
memory_trick: FIRST OF ALL → THEN → FINALLY.
visual_association: A numbered list starting with 1.
confusing_word: first of all vs at first
difference_explained: First of all = the first point in a list. At first = at the beginning (then it changed).
related_words: firstly, to begin with, at first
mini_conversation: A: How do I start the machine? / B: First of all, plug it in.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'First of all, wash your hands.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'First of all, the minister thanked the rescue teams.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'First of all, who ate my Maggi?'
mcq_question: Choose: '___, I'd like to welcome our guests.'
mcq_options: A) At first  B) First of all  C) In first  D) First of
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___ ___, let me say sorry. → First of all
find_and_fix_to_correct: At first, I want to thank my parents. (starting a speech) → First of all, I want to thank my parents.
translate: सबसे पहले, आने के लिए धन्यवाद। → First of all, thank you for coming.
write_your_own_sentence: Write the first line of a speech using 'First of all'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'before anything else; used to start a list of points'?
usage_tip: Use 'First of all… Then… Finally…' to order your points.

simple_explanation: At the beginning (before something changed).
example_1: At first, I didn't like her.
example_2: At first it was hard, but now it's easy.
example_3: At first, nobody believed him.
collocations: at first, but later
grammar_pattern: At first, + clause, but + later change
common_mistake: At first of all, I was scared.
correct_version: At first, I was scared.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At first' has no 'of all'.
etymology: at + first.
mnemonic: 'Shuru mein' = at first.
memory_trick: AT FIRST … BUT NOW — a change.
visual_association: A seed, then a flower.
confusing_word: at first vs first of all
difference_explained: At first = in the beginning, then it changed. First of all = the first point in a list.
related_words: initially, in the beginning, first of all
mini_conversation: A: Do you like your new school? / B: At first, no — but now I love it.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'At first, cooking was hard for me.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'At first, officials denied the report.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'At first I thought you were joking!'
mcq_question: Choose: ___, I was nervous, but then I relaxed.
mcq_options: A) First of all  B) At first  C) In first  D) Firstly of
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___, the city felt strange to me. → At first
find_and_fix_to_correct: In first, I didn't understand. → At first, I didn't understand.
translate: शुरू में मुझे डर लगा। → At first, I was scared.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about something that was hard at first.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'at the beginning (before something changed)'?
usage_tip: 'At first' needs a later change — 'but now…' or 'later…'.

simple_explanation: Immediately; also, at the same time.
example_2: I can't do two things at once.
example_3: The doctor came at once.
collocations: at once, all at once
grammar_pattern: verb + at once
common_mistake: Come at once immediately.
correct_version: Come at once. / Come immediately.
why_it_s_wrong: 'At once' and 'immediately' mean the same — use one.
etymology: at + once.
word_family: once, at once, all at once
mnemonic: 'Turant' = at once.
memory_trick: AT ONCE = right now OR together.
visual_association: A siren on an ambulance.
difference_explained: At once = immediately. Once = one time (I went there once).
mini_conversation: A: The kitchen is on fire! / B: Call the fire brigade at once!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Everyone started talking at once.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Police reached the spot at once.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I can't eat all this at once!'
mcq_options: A) at once  B) one time  C) once at  D) at one
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Please reply ___ ___. → at once
find_and_fix_to_correct: Do it at once time. → Do it at once.
translate: तुरंत यहाँ आओ! → Come here at once!
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a time you had to act at once.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'immediately; also, at the same time'?
usage_tip: 'All at once' = suddenly: 'All at once, the lights went off.'

memory_trick: MORE OR LESS = almost.

mini_conversation: A: Is the report ready? / B: More or less — just the last page.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'We live more or less near each other.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Prices stayed more or less the same.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'I'm more or less ready!'
mcq_question: Choose: The two phones are ___ the same.
mcq_options: A) more and less  B) more or less  C) most or less  D) more of less
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The house is ___ ___ ___ ready. → more or less
find_and_fix_to_correct: It is less or more ₹1,000. → It is more or less ₹1,000.

write_your_own_sentence: Write about something that is more or less finished.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'almost; approximately'?
usage_tip: 'Roughly' and 'about' are common alternatives with numbers.

simple_explanation: Slowly, in small amounts.
example_1: Little by little, my English is improving.
example_2: Add the water little by little.
example_3: Little by little, she got better.
collocations: little by little
grammar_pattern: Little by little, + clause / verb + little by little
common_mistake: Little little my English is improving.
correct_version: Little by little, my English is improving.

common_mistake: On the way, I saw your brother yesterday. (meaning 'by the way')
correct_version: By the way, I saw your brother yesterday.
why_it_s_wrong: 'On the way' = while travelling. 'By the way' = changing topic.
etymology: by + the + way.
word_family: way, by the way, on the way
mnemonic: 'Waise' = by the way.
memory_trick: BTW = By The Way.
visual_association: A speech bubble with 'BTW'.
confusing_word: by the way vs on the way
difference_explained: By the way = changing topic. On the way = while going somewhere.
mini_conversation: A: See you tomorrow. / B: Oh, by the way, bring my book!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'By the way, the meeting is at four, not three.'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'BTW, you look great!'
mcq_question: Choose: '___, did you get my message?'
mcq_options: A) On the way  B) By the way  C) In the way  D) By way
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___ ___, where do you live? → By the way
find_and_fix_to_correct: By the way I am going to office, I saw him. → On the way to the office, I saw him.

write_your_own_sentence: Write a message that uses 'By the way' to add something.

simple_explanation: Don't worry about it; it's not important.
example_2: Never mind, I'll do it myself.
example_3: Never mind the cost.
collocations: never mind, oh never mind
grammar_pattern: Never mind (+ noun)
common_mistake: Don't mind, it's okay.
correct_version: Never mind, it's okay.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Don't mind' is Indian English for this; the standard phrase is 'never mind'.
etymology: never + mind.
mnemonic: 'Koi baat nahi' = never mind.
memory_trick: NEVER MIND = forget it, no problem.
visual_association: A person waving a hand, smiling.
difference_explained: Never mind = it's okay, forget it. 'I don't mind' = it's fine with me.
related_words: forget it, no problem, it doesn't matter
mini_conversation: A: Sorry, I can't find the photo. / B: Never mind, it's not important.
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Never mind, we'll take the next bus.'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Oh, never mind — I found it!'
mcq_question: Choose: 'Sorry, I broke your pencil.' '___, I have another one.'
mcq_options: A) Don't mind  B) Never mind  C) No mind  D) Mind never
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: '___ ___, it happens.' → Never mind
find_and_fix_to_correct: Don't mind, I will buy another one. → Never mind, I'll buy another one.
translate: कोई बात नहीं, मैं खुद कर लूँगा। → Never mind, I'll do it myself.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a reply using 'Never mind' to a friend's apology.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'don't worry about it; it's not important'?
usage_tip: 'Never mind' also means 'forget what I just said'.

simple_explanation: Used to agree to a suggestion, or to make one.
example_2: Why not try the new café?
example_3: Why not ask the teacher?
collocations: why not, why don't we
grammar_pattern: Why not? (reply) / Why not + base verb?
common_mistake: Why not to try again?
correct_version: Why not try again?
why_it_s_wrong: After 'why not', use the base verb — no 'to'.
etymology: why + not.
mnemonic: 'Kyon nahi?' = why not?
memory_trick: WHY NOT + base verb.
visual_association: A thumbs-up with a smile.
confusing_word: why not vs why don't you
difference_explained: Why not + verb = short suggestion. Why don't you + verb = the same, longer.
mini_conversation: A: Pizza tonight? / B: Why not?
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Why not take a short break?'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Sure, why not!'
mcq_options: A) Why not to  B) Why not  C) Why don't to  D) Why no
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: '___ ___ take the metro? It's faster.' → Why not
find_and_fix_to_correct: Why not we go for a movie? → Why don't we go for a movie? / Why not go for a movie?
translate: क्यों नहीं? चलो चलते हैं। → Why not? Let's go.
write_your_own_sentence: Write a suggestion starting with 'Why not…?'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to agree to a suggestion, or to make one'?
usage_tip: 'Why not?' with rising tone = 'Sure!'

simple_explanation: Used to make a suggestion or ask someone's opinion.
example_1: How about a cup of tea?
example_2: How about going to the beach?
example_3: I'm fine. How about you?
collocations: how about + -ing, how about you
grammar_pattern: How about + noun / -ing?
common_mistake: How about go to the park?
correct_version: How about going to the park?
why_it_s_wrong: After 'how about', use a noun or -ing.
etymology: how + about.
mnemonic: 'Kaisa rahega?' = how about?
memory_trick: HOW ABOUT + -ING.
visual_association: Two friends looking at a map.
difference_explained: Same for suggestions. 'What about…?' can also point to a problem ('What about the cost?').
mini_conversation: A: I'm bored. / B: How about watching a movie?
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'How about meeting at six?'
news_style_line: News-style: (not used in formal news)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'How about you, what's new?'
mcq_question: Choose: How about ___ out for dinner?
mcq_options: A) go  B) going  C) to go  D) went
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: ___ ___ a walk after dinner? → How about
find_and_fix_to_correct: How about we are going to Goa? → How about going to Goa?
translate: चलो आइसक्रीम खाएँ, कैसा रहेगा? → How about some ice cream?
write_your_own_sentence: Write two suggestions with 'How about…?'.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'used to make a suggestion or ask someone's opinion'?
usage_tip: 'How about you?' = And you? (returning a question).

simple_explanation: A polite way to ask someone to repeat what they said.
example_2: Pardon me, is this seat taken?
example_3: I beg your pardon?
collocations: pardon me, I beg your pardon
grammar_pattern: Pardon? / Pardon me
word_forms: pardon (also a verb and noun: to forgive officially)
common_mistake: What? Say again.
correct_version: Pardon? / Sorry, could you say that again?
why_it_s_wrong: 'What?' can sound rude; 'Pardon?' is polite.
etymology: Old French 'pardoner' (to forgive).
mnemonic: 'Kya kaha? (politely)' = Pardon?
memory_trick: PARDON? = please repeat.
visual_association: A person cupping a hand to their ear.
difference_explained: Both can ask for a repeat. 'Sorry?' is more common today; 'Pardon?' is a little more formal.
mini_conversation: A: The train leaves at nine-fifty. / B: Pardon? Nine-fifteen or nine-fifty?
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'Pardon me, can I get past?'
news_style_line: News-style: 'The President pardoned the prisoner.' (= forgave officially)
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Pardon my French!' (= sorry for swearing)
mcq_question: Choose the most polite way to ask someone to repeat:
mcq_options: A) What?  B) Huh?  C) Pardon?  D) Say again!
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: '___? I didn't catch that.' → Pardon
find_and_fix_to_correct: Once more say it. → Pardon? / Could you say that again, please?
translate: माफ़ कीजिए, आपने क्या कहा? → Pardon?
write_your_own_sentence: Write two polite ways to ask someone to repeat.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'a polite way to ask someone to repeat what they said'?
usage_tip: 'I beg your pardon?' with a sharp tone means you're offended.

simple_explanation: What you say to someone on their birthday.
example_2: Wish him a happy birthday.
example_3: Happy birthday to you!
collocations: wish someone a happy birthday, belated happy birthday
grammar_pattern: Happy birthday (+ name) / wish + person + a happy birthday
common_mistake: Many many happy returns of the day and happy birthday to you from my side.
correct_version: Happy birthday! Have a wonderful day.
why_it_s_wrong: Keep it short and natural — long Indian-English strings can sound odd abroad.
spelling_tip: HAPPY BIRTHDAY: two words (BIRTHDAY is one word).
etymology: happy + birth + day.
mnemonic: 'Janamdin mubarak' = happy birthday.
memory_trick: BIRTHDAY is one word.
visual_association: A cake with candles.
confusing_word: happy birthday vs many happy returns
difference_explained: Both are birthday wishes. 'Many happy returns' is old-fashioned and mostly Indian or British.
mini_conversation: A: Happy birthday, Dad! / B: Thank you, beta!
everyday_scene: Everyday: 'We sang happy birthday at midnight.'
news_style_line: News-style: 'Fans wished the actor a happy birthday online.'
casual_conversation: Casual: 'HBD, bro!'
mcq_question: Choose: What do you say to a friend on their birthday?
mcq_options: A) Congratulations  B) Happy birthday  C) Get well soon  D) Best of luck
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: '___ ___! Here's your gift.' → Happy birthday
find_and_fix_to_correct: Happy birth day to you. → Happy birthday to you.
translate: जन्मदिन मुबारक हो! → Happy birthday!
write_your_own_sentence: Write a short birthday message to a friend.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'what you say to someone on their birthday'?
usage_tip: 'Belated happy birthday' = sorry this wish is late.

simple_explanation: Working without wires.
example_2: Is there wireless internet here?
example_3: This mouse is wireless.
collocations: wireless earphones, wireless internet, wireless mouse, wireless charger
grammar_pattern: wireless + noun / be wireless
common_mistake: I have wire less earphones.
correct_version: I have wireless earphones.
why_it_s_wrong: One word: wireless.
spelling_tip: WIRE + LESS: keep the E in 'wire' — wireless, not 'wirless'.
etymology: Formed in English from wire + -less.
mnemonic: WIRE-LESS = no WIRES.
memory_trick: Old use: 'wireless' once meant 'radio'.
visual_association: Earbuds in a small charging case.
difference_explained: Bluetooth = one type of short-range wireless connection.
mini_conversation:
A: Why no cable for your speaker?
B: It's wireless — it uses Bluetooth.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The village school got wireless internet for its computer lab.
news_style_line: News-style: Wireless charging is becoming common in phones.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Wireless earphones. Lost one in a week.'
mcq_options: A) wireless  B) wire less  C) wiring  D) wirelessly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: The phone charges ______. → wirelessly
find_and_fix_to_correct: He bought wire less mouse. → He bought a wireless mouse.
translate: मैंने वायरलेस ईयरफ़ोन ख़रीदे। → I bought wireless earphones.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a wireless device you use daily.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'working without wires'?
usage_tip: Opposite: wired.

simple_explanation: Connected to or done on the internet.
example_2: Online shopping is popular.
example_3: She's online right now.
collocations: online class, online payment, online shopping, go online, be online
grammar_pattern: online + noun (adj) / verb + online (adv) / be online
common_mistake: I did online payment.
correct_version: I paid online. / I made an online payment.
why_it_s_wrong: Use 'pay online' or 'make an online payment'.
spelling_tip: ON + LINE: one word, no hyphen.
etymology: Formed in English from on + line.
mnemonic: ONLINE → you're ON the internet LINE.
memory_trick: Works as adjective ('online class') and adverb ('study online').
visual_association: A student attending a class on a laptop at home.
difference_explained: Digital = electronic. Online = connected to the internet.
mini_conversation:
A: How do you study English?
B: Mostly online — videos and apps.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The farmer sells his honey online now.
news_style_line: News-style: Online fraud cases are rising, police warn.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Online all day. Productive: 10 minutes.'
mcq_options: A) online  B) on line  C) onlinely  D) in online
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Is the shop open, or only ______? → online
find_and_fix_to_correct: I did online booking of tickets. → I booked tickets online.
translate: मैं ऑनलाइन क्लास लेता हूँ। → I take online classes.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about your favourite online learning tool.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'on the internet'?
usage_tip: Opposite: offline.

simple_explanation: Not connected to the internet; done in person.
example_2: The website is offline for repairs.
example_3: We'll discuss this offline.
collocations: go offline, work offline, offline mode, offline class, discuss offline
grammar_pattern: be offline / offline + noun / verb + offline
common_mistake: My phone is in offline.
correct_version: My phone is offline.
why_it_s_wrong: No 'in' — just 'is offline'.
spelling_tip: OFF + LINE: one word, double F.
etymology: Formed in English from off + line.
mnemonic: OFFLINE → OFF the internet LINE.
memory_trick: Office use: 'Let's take this offline' = discuss privately later.
visual_association: A phone showing 'No internet — offline mode'.
difference_explained: Out of network = no mobile signal. Offline = not connected to the internet.
mini_conversation:
A: Can I use the dictionary on the train?
B: Yes, it works offline.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The village kiosk runs an offline version of the app.
news_style_line: News-style: The booking site went offline for two hours.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Went offline for a day. Survived. Barely.'
mcq_question: 'Download the map so you can use it ___.'
mcq_options: A) offline  B) in offline  C) off line  D) offlined
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Our classes are both online and ______. → offline
find_and_fix_to_correct: The site is in offline. → The site is offline.
translate: ऐप बिना इंटरनेट के चलता है। → The app works offline.
write_your_own_sentence: Write why offline apps are useful in villages.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which word means 'not connected to the internet'?
usage_tip: Offline-first is great design for India.

simple_explanation: Light and small enough to carry easily.
example_2: This fan is portable.
example_3: A laptop is more portable than a desktop.
collocations: portable charger, portable speaker, portable fan, portable device
grammar_pattern: be portable / portable + noun
common_mistake: We need portable water in villages.
correct_version: We need drinking (potable) water in villages.
why_it_s_wrong: PORTABLE = easy to carry. POTABLE = safe to drink.
etymology: From Latin portare, 'to carry'.
mnemonic: PORT-ABLE → ABLE to be carried (port = carry, like a PORTer).
memory_trick: Trap: portable ≠ potable.
visual_association: A small speaker clipped to a backpack.
difference_explained: Mobile = can move or be moved. Portable = small enough to carry by hand.
mini_conversation:
A: My phone always dies on trips.
B: Buy a portable charger — a power bank.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The travelling doctor carries a portable BP machine.
news_style_line: News-style: Portable solar lamps are helping remote villages.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Portable snacks = my travel essential.'
mcq_options: A) portable  B) potable  C) portabled  D) port
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Clean, ______ water is a basic need. → potable (drinking)
find_and_fix_to_correct: Carry portable water on the trek. → Carry drinking water on the trek.
translate: मैंने पोर्टेबल स्पीकर ख़रीदा। → I bought a portable speaker.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a portable device you use on trips.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'easy to carry'?
usage_tip: Don't confuse with 'potable' (safe to drink).

simple_explanation: Old-fashioned; no longer useful or modern.
example_2: These rules are outdated.
example_3: The map was outdated.
collocations: outdated software, outdated rules, outdated ideas, outdated information
grammar_pattern: be outdated / outdated + noun
common_mistake: My phone is old dated.
correct_version: My phone is outdated.
why_it_s_wrong: The word is 'outdated' (one word).
etymology: Formed in English from out + dated.
mnemonic: OUT-DATED → OUT of DATE.
memory_trick: After a verb: 'out of date'; before a noun: 'outdated'.
visual_association: An old flip phone next to a new smartphone.
difference_explained: Old = has existed a long time. Outdated = no longer useful or current.
mini_conversation:
A: Why won't the app install?
B: Your phone's software is outdated.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The village clinic replaced its outdated equipment.
news_style_line: News-style: Experts called the exam syllabus outdated.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'My jokes are outdated. So am I.'
mcq_options: A) outdated  B) old dated  C) out date  D) dated out
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: This information is out of ______. → date
find_and_fix_to_correct: This map is old dated. → This map is outdated.
translate: मेरा फ़ोन पुराना हो गया है। → My phone is outdated.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about something outdated in your school or office.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'old-fashioned, no longer useful'?
usage_tip: Opposite: up-to-date.

simple_explanation: Modern; having the latest information.
example_1: Keep your apps up to date.
example_2: We need up-to-date information.
example_3: She's always up to date with the news.
collocations: up-to-date information, keep up to date, stay up to date, up-to-date software
grammar_pattern: up-to-date + noun (hyphens) / be/keep + up to date (no hyphens)
common_mistake: Keep your apps update.
correct_version: Keep your apps up to date (or updated).
why_it_s_wrong: 'Update' is a verb/noun. Use 'up to date' or 'updated'.
spelling_tip: UP-TO-DATE: two hyphens before a noun (an up-to-date list); no hyphens after a verb (keep it up to date).
etymology: Everyday words: up + to + date.
mnemonic: UP TO DATE = UP TO today's DATE.
memory_trick: Hyphens before a noun only: 'up-to-date news' but 'The news is up to date.'
visual_association: A phone showing 'Your software is up to date ✔'.
difference_explained: New = recently made. Up-to-date = has the latest information or version.
mini_conversation:
A: Is this price list correct?
B: Yes, it's up to date — updated today.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The panchayat keeps up-to-date records of every family.
news_style_line: News-style: Farmers get up-to-date weather alerts on their phones.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'My knowledge of cricket is up to date. Studies, not so much.'
mcq_options: A) up to date  B) update  C) up-to-dated  D) up the date
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: I read the news daily to stay ______. → up to date
find_and_fix_to_correct: Keep your phone update. → Keep your phone up to date.
translate: अपने ऐप्स अपडेट रखो। → Keep your apps up to date.
write_your_own_sentence: Write how you keep your English up to date.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'modern, with the latest information'?
usage_tip: Opposite: outdated.

hindi_meaning: (ऑनलाइन) तेज़ी से फैलने वाला; वायरस से होने वाला
simple_explanation: (Of online content) spreading fast to many people; caused by a virus.

correct_version: The video went viral.

mnemonic: VIRAL → spreads like a VIRUS from person to person.
memory_trick: Two meanings: online popularity and virus-related illness.
visual_association: A phone showing a video with millions of views.
difference_explained: Trending = popular right now. Viral = spreading extremely fast to huge numbers.
mini_conversation:
A: How did the chaiwala become famous?

news_style_line: News-style: Police warned about a viral fake message on WhatsApp.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Posted a video. It went viral in my family group. 12 views.'

find_and_fix_to_correct: His post got viraled on Twitter. → His post went viral on Twitter.
translate: वीडियो वायरल हो गया। → The video went viral.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about a viral video that inspired you.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'spreading fast online'?
usage_tip: Your YouTube goal: go viral!

simple_explanation: Safe from danger or attack; stable and certain.

example_3: He has a secure government job.

common_mistake: Is this site secured?

why_it_s_wrong: For 'safe', the adjective is 'secure'. 'Secured' = made safe by someone.
etymology: From Latin securus, 'free from care'.
mnemonic: SECURE → free from worry, like a locked SAFE.
memory_trick: Web tip: look for 'https' and the padlock icon.
visual_association: A padlock icon next to a website address.
difference_explained: Safe = not in danger. Secure = protected (often by locks or systems), or stable.
mini_conversation:

everyday_scene: Everyday: The farmer keeps his papers in a secure steel box.
news_style_line: News-style: Banks are making online payments more secure.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Secure in my blanket. Nothing can touch me.'
mcq_options: A) secure  B) security  C) securely  D) secured to
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Online ______ is very important. → security
find_and_fix_to_correct: Is this app secured for payment? → Is this app secure for payment?
translate: क्या यह वेबसाइट सुरक्षित है? → Is this website secure?
write_your_own_sentence: Write three ways to keep your phone secure.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
reverse_quick_recall: Which adjective means 'safe from danger or attack'?
usage_tip: Opposite: insecure (also = lacking confidence).

news_style_line: News-style: Experts say users should protect their privacy online.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Private moment: eating chocolate in the fridge light.'
mcq_options: A) private  B) privately in  C) privacy  D) privet

find_and_fix_to_correct: Keep this information privately. → Keep this information private.

write_your_own_sentence: Write two settings to keep your social media private.

simple_explanation: Done online or by computer, not physically; almost the same as.
example_2: The museum offers a virtual tour.
example_3: It was a virtual certainty.
collocations: virtual meeting, virtual class, virtual tour, virtual reality (VR)

hindi_meaning: अस्वास्थ्यकर, सेहत के लिए बुरा; बीमार
simple_explanation: Bad for your health; not in good health.
example_2: He looks pale and unhealthy.
example_3: It's an unhealthy habit.
collocations: unhealthy food, unhealthy habit, unhealthy lifestyle, unhealthy relationship
grammar_pattern: be unhealthy / unhealthy + noun
common_mistake: Junk food is not healthy for health.
correct_version: Junk food is unhealthy.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Not healthy for health' repeats itself. Just say 'unhealthy'.
etymology: From un- + 'healthy' (health, Old English hælth).
mnemonic: UN-HEALTHY → NOT good for your HEALTH.
memory_trick: Also for relationships: 'an unhealthy friendship'.
visual_association: A plate of fries and soda next to a sad heart icon.
synonyms: bad for you, harmful, junk; unwell
difference_explained: Ill = sick now. Unhealthy = bad for health, or not in good health generally.
mini_conversation:
A: Why no cold drinks?
B: They're unhealthy — too much sugar.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The doctor warned the farmer about his unhealthy habit of skipping meals.
news_style_line: News-style: Experts say sitting all day is unhealthy.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Unhealthy relationship with samosas. Can't quit.'
mcq_options: A) unhealthy  B) not healthy for health  C) unhealth  D) unhealthily
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: Too much screen time is an ______ habit. → unhealthy
find_and_fix_to_correct: Smoking is not healthy for health. → Smoking is unhealthy.
translate: जंक फ़ूड सेहत के लिए बुरा है। → Junk food is unhealthy.
write_your_own_sentence: Write about an unhealthy habit you want to change.

usage_tip: Opposite: healthy.

simple_explanation: In a way related to the body; in reality.
example_2: The job is physically tiring.
example_3: It's physically impossible to be in two places at once.
collocations: physically fit, physically active, physically tired, physically impossible, physically disabled
grammar_pattern: physically + adjective / verb + physically
common_mistake: He is physically handicapped.
correct_version: He is physically disabled. / He has a physical disability.
why_it_s_wrong: 'Handicapped' is old and can offend; 'disabled' or 'person with a disability' is respectful.
spelling_tip: PHYSICAL + LY: double L — physicaLLy. PH sounds like F.
etymology: From 'physical', from Greek physis, 'nature', + -ly.
mnemonic: PHYSICALLY → about the body (PHYSIQUE).
memory_trick: Respectful English: 'person with a disability'.
visual_association: A person doing push-ups in a park.
difference_explained: Physically = about the body. Mentally = about the mind.
mini_conversation:
A: How's the new warehouse job?
B: Physically hard, but the pay is good.
everyday_scene: Everyday: The old farmer is still physically strong at 80.
news_style_line: News-style: Doctors say children should be physically active every day.
casual_conversation: Casual: 'Physically at work. Mentally on holiday.'
mcq_options: A) physically  B) physical  C) physics  D) physicly
fill_in_the_blank_to_answer: He is ______ tired but mentally fresh. → physically
find_and_fix_to_correct: He is physical fit. → He is physically fit.
translate: वह शारीरिक रूप से फ़िट है। → He's physically fit.
write_your_own_sentence: Write three ways to stay physically active.
spaced_repetition_plan: Day 1 learn → Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14 → Day 30 review
